summary: Plans multiple zeta values over F_q[θ] after Ngo Dac (Annals 2021), Chang–Chen–Mishiba (Forum Math. Pi 2023) and Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham (Forum Math. Pi 2024), as a Part II of DrinfeldModulesAndTModules. MZ.0 defines indices and arrays, the power sums of both realisations, Thakur’s values ζ_A(s), Harada’s alternating values, Carlitz multiple polylogarithms, Carlitz’s identity on Thakur’s range, the index families I^T_w, I^0_w, IND_w, AS_w with their counts d(w), s(w), and ζ_A(q − 1) = −π̃^{q−1}/D_1. MZ.1 gives Chen’s formula, the harmonic and q-shuffle products on the index space and the multiplicativity of the realisations. MZ.2 gives binary relations, Thakur’s relation R_1, Todd’s operators, the reduction to admissible indices and Brown’s theorem in positive characteristic, the rewriting operator U^• with the IND_w generating set, the strong Brown theorem for ACMPLs and the bridges AZ_w = AL_w, Z_w = L_w. MZ.3 gives the Anderson–Thakur polynomials, Chang’s deformation series and dual t-motives, the MZ property and Chang’s descent theorem, and the ABP independence criterion with the Eulerian suffix constraint. MZ.4 solves the Frobenius difference systems: monic descent, the θ-degree bound, the key lemma and dim X_w ∈ {0, 1}. MZ.5 proves Ngo Dac’s Theorems B and D, the CMPL basis, Thakur’s basis theorem with dim_K Z_w = d(w), all linear relations, the Hoffman-like basis and dim_K AZ_w = s(w), with the small-weight AMZV bounds and the v-adic bound.

nodes.title: Indices, arrays and their orders
nodes.statement: An index is a finite list s = (s_1, …, s_r) of positive integers, r ≥ 0, with weight wt(s) = s_1 + ⋯ + s_r and depth dep(s) = r; the empty index ∅ has weight and depth 0, and s_i := 0 for i > r is used only in comparisons. For nonempty s put s_+ = (s_1, …, s_{r−1}) and s_− = (s_2, …, s_r); (s, t) is concatenation, and q^{{m}} denotes m consecutive entries q. Prefix dominance: s ≤ t iff wt(s) = wt(t) and s_1 + ⋯ + s_i ≤ t_1 + ⋯ + t_i for every i ≥ 1. The collapse T_i(s) = (s_1 + ⋯ + s_i, s_{i+1}, …, s_r) (i ≥ 1, so T_1(s) = s), and s + t is the coordinatewise sum of the zero-padded sequences, trailing zeros dropped (not concatenation). For a fixed prime power q, Init(s) = (s_1, …, s_i) with i maximal such that s_1, …, s_i ≤ q, and initial tuples are compared in the lexicographic order of finite lists, a proper prefix being smaller. For k ≥ 1, s is k-admissible iff s_1, …, s_k ≤ q (zero-padded) and s is not of the form (s_1, …, s_r) with r ≤ k, s_1, …, s_{r−1} ≤ q and s_r = q; ∅ is k-admissible. An array (ε; s) is an index s of depth r together with ε = (ε_1, …, ε_r) ∈ (F_q^×)^r; its character is χ(ε) = ε_1⋯ε_r, the sum of arrays is (εε′; s + t) with ε_i := 1 past the depth, and (ε; s) ≤ (ε′; t) iff χ(ε) = χ(ε′) and s ≤ t (a preorder).
hypotheses: q = p^e a fixed prime power; entries of indices are positive integers.
proofSteps: Represent an index as a list of positive integers; weight and depth are its sum and length.

Prefix dominance is reflexive and transitive, and antisymmetric among indices of one weight; if s ≤ t then (u, s) ≤ (u, t), u + s ≤ u + t, T_k(s) ≤ T_k(t) for every k, and dep(s) ≥ dep(t) (Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham Remark 1.1: a shorter index of the same weight would have a strictly smaller final prefix sum).
If T_i(s) ≤ T_i(t) then T_k(s) ≤ T_k(t) for all k ≥ i (Ngo Dac §2.1).
For integers x > i > 0, (x − i, (i) + c) ≤ (x, c); for nonempty a and any b, (a_1, a_− + b) ≤ a + b; these are the support bounds used by the product expansions.
An index of weight w ≥ 1 is w-admissible iff it lies in Thakur's family I^T_w (entries ≤ q, last entry < q).
acceptance: (1, 2) ≤ (2, 1) but (2, 1) is not ≤ (1, 2); (1, 3) and (2, 1, 1) are incomparable although (1, 3) precedes (2, 1, 1) lexicographically.
Init(q + 1, 1) = ∅ and Init(q, q, 1) = (q, q, 1); (q) is not 1-admissible while (q, 1) is.

nodes.title: Power sums of both realisations
nodes.statement:
Let A = F_q[θ], K = F_q(θ), A_{+,d} the finite set of monic polynomials of degree d, ℓ_0 = 1 and ℓ_d = ∏_{i=1}^{d}(θ − θ^{q^i}). For d ∈ Z and an array (ε; s) of depth r ≥ 1 put
S_d(ε; s) = Σ ε_1^{deg a_1}⋯ε_r^{deg a_r} a_1^{−s_1}⋯a_r^{−s_r} ∈ K, over a_i ∈ A_+ with d = deg a_1 > ⋯ > deg a_r ≥ 0,
Si_d(ε; s) = Σ ε_1^{d_1}⋯ε_r^{d_r} ℓ_{d_1}^{−s_1}⋯ℓ_{d_r}^{−s_r} ∈ K, over integers d = d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0,
both zero when d < r − 1, and S_{<d} = Σ_{0 ≤ j < d} S_j, Si_{<d} = Σ_{0 ≤ j < d} Si_j for nonempty arrays. For the empty array, S_{<d}(∅) = Si_{<d}(∅) = 1 for every d ∈ Z, and S_d(∅) = Si_d(∅) is 1 for d = 0 and 0 otherwise. Trivial characters give S_d(s), Si_d(s). One has S_d(ε; s) = S_d(ε_1; s_1) S_{<d}(ε_−; s_−), Si_d(ε; s) = Si_d(ε_1; s_1) Si_{<d}(ε_−; s_−), S_d(ε; s) = ε^d S_d(s) and Si_d(ε; s) = ε^d ℓ_d^{−s} in depth one for d ≥ 0.
hypotheses: θ transcendental over F_q, so the sums lie in K = F_q(θ); ε_i ∈ F_q^×.
proofSteps: For d ≥ 0, A_{+,d} has q^d elements; for d < 0 it is empty. Thus every S_d is a finite sum in K; Si_d is a finite sum over decreasing nonnegative integer sequences below d.

The factorisations follow by separating the first summation variable; the convention S_{<d}(∅) = 1 for every d ∈ Z is what makes the depth-one case d = 0 of the factorisation correct (source issue E1 records the slip of the opposite convention).
In depth one, ε^{deg a} = ε^d for every a ∈ A_{+,d}, and ε^{d_1} = ε^d, giving the character factor.

Defines S_d, S_<d, Si_d, Si_<d for tuples and for arrays, with the elementary identities Si_d(ε; s) = ε^d Si_d(s) in depth one and the factorisation of Si_d.

nodes.title: Thakur multiple zeta values
nodes.statement: For an index s of depth r ≥ 1, Thakur's multiple zeta value is ζ_A(s) = Σ_{d ≥ 0} S_d(s) ∈ K_∞ = F_q((1/θ)), that is the sum of a_1^{−s_1}⋯a_r^{−s_r} over monic a_1, …, a_r with deg a_1 > ⋯ > deg a_r. The series converges since |S_d(s)|_∞ ≤ q^{−d s_1} (|·|_∞ normalised by |θ|_∞ = q); ζ_A(∅) = 1. Its weight and depth are those of s; in depth one these are the Carlitz zeta values ζ_A(n) = Σ_{a ∈ A_+} a^{−n}.
hypotheses: The valuation at ∞ normalised by v_∞(θ) = −1; K_∞ is the completion of K at ∞.
proofSteps: Each term a_1^{−s_1}⋯a_r^{−s_r} with deg a_1 = d has absolute value at most q^{−d s_1}, and an ultrametric finite sum is bounded by its largest term, so |S_d(s)|_∞ ≤ q^{−d s_1} → 0.
Hence the series converges (unconditionally) in K_∞ and equals the sum over strictly degree-decreasing tuples of monic polynomials.
The acceptance identity at 1 uses DM.6/small-power-sum with exponent 1 and the logarithm series of DM.2/carlitz-exponential; 1 is inside its convergence disc.
acceptance: ζ_A(1) = Σ_{d ≥ 0} ℓ_d^{−1} = log_C(1) (DM.6/small-power-sum).
For q = 2, ζ_A(1)² = ζ_A(2), since squaring is additive in characteristic 2.

The trivial character recovers Thakur’s values.

nodes.title: Thakur’s nonvanishing theorem
nodes.statement: For every prime power q and every index s of positive depth, ζ_A(s) ≠ 0; likewise ζ_A(ε; s) ≠ 0 for every array. More precisely, if for each k ≥ 1 the degrees deg_θ S_d(k) (d ≥ 0) are finite and strictly decreasing in d, then the term S_{r−1}(s_1)S_{r−2}(s_2)⋯S_0(s_r) is the unique term of largest degree in Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0} S_{d_1}(s_1)⋯S_{d_r}(s_r).
hypotheses: s of depth r ≥ 1; q any prime power.
proofSteps: For 1 ≤ k ≤ q, S_d(k) = ℓ_d^{−k} has degree −k(q + q² + ⋯ + q^d), which is strictly decreasing in d (DM.6/small-power-sum).

For general k, Thakur shows S_d(k) ≠ 0 and −deg S_d(k) strictly increasing in d: for q prime from his recursion for the degrees, and for general q from the minimal-decomposition formula or Sheats’s degree inequality (Thakur 2009, proof of Theorem 4). This general-q degree input is recorded as a gap.

Given strict monotonicity, the degree of S_{d_1}(s_1)⋯S_{d_r}(s_r) over d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0 is uniquely maximised at d_i = r − i, so no cancellation can occur and ζ_A(s) ≠ 0; the character factors have absolute value 1, so the same argument applies to ζ_A(ε; s).
acceptance: ζ_A(1) has leading term 1; for q = 2, ζ_A(1, 1) has leading term S_1(1) = (θ² + θ)^{−1} of degree −2.

nodes.title: Carlitz multiple polylogarithms
nodes.statement: For an index s of depth r ≥ 1, the Carlitz multiple polylogarithm is the series Li_s(z_1, …, z_r) = Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0} z_1^{q^{d_1}}⋯z_r^{q^{d_r}} / (ℓ_{d_1}^{s_1}⋯ℓ_{d_r}^{s_r}), converging on its domain D_s ⊂ C_∞^r, which contains the polydisc D′_s = {|z_i|_∞ < q^{s_i q/(q−1)}}. Its values at 1 are Li(s) = Li_s(1, …, 1) = Σ_{d ≥ 0} Si_d(s) ∈ K_∞, with Li(∅) = 1; for an array, Li(ε; s) = Σ_{d ≥ 0} Si_d(ε; s) ∈ K_∞ (alternating Carlitz multiple polylogarithm). If γ_i ∈ F̄_q satisfies γ_i^{q−1} = ε_i, then Li_s(γ_1, …, γ_r) = γ_1⋯γ_r Li(ε; s). In depth one Li_n is Anderson–Thakur’s n-th Carlitz polylogarithm and Li_1 = log_C.
hypotheses: C_∞ and its absolute value from DM.2; ℓ_d from DM.0.
proofSteps: |ℓ_i^n|_∞ = q^{nq(q^i − 1)/(q − 1)} (from the product defining ℓ_i and |θ|_∞ = q), so the general term has absolute value q^{q(s_1 + ⋯ + s_r)/(q−1)} ∏_j |z_j/θ^{q s_j/(q−1)}|^{q^{d_j}}, which tends to 0 on D′_s (Chang (5.1.2) and Remark 5.1.4).
For γ^{q−1} = ε one has γ^{q^d} = γ·ε^{(q^d − 1)/(q − 1)} = γ ε^d, because 1 + q + ⋯ + q^{d−1} ≡ d mod q − 1.
Hence Li_s(γ) = Σ γ_1 ε_1^{d_1}⋯γ_r ε_r^{d_r}/(ℓ_{d_1}^{s_1}⋯) = γ_1⋯γ_r Li(ε; s).
acceptance: Li_1(z) = Σ_d z^{q^d}/ℓ_d = log_C(z), and Li(1) = log_C(1) = ζ_A(1).

nodes.title: Nonvanishing of Carlitz polylogarithm values
nodes.statement: For an index s of depth r ≥ 1 and u ∈ D′_s with every u_i ≠ 0, the general term of Li_s(u) has a unique term of largest absolute value, at (d_1, …, d_r) = (r − 1, …, 0); hence Li_s(u) ≠ 0. In particular Li(s) ≠ 0 and Li(ε; s) ≠ 0 for every array, and 𝔏-type normalised values γ_1⋯γ_r Li(ε; s)/π̃^{wt(s)} are nonzero.
proofSteps: By the absolute value of the general term in MZ.0/carlitz-multiple-polylogarithm, each factor |u_j/θ^{q s_j/(q−1)}| is < 1, so raising it to q^{d_j} with d_j as small as possible maximises the term; the strictly decreasing constraint forces d_j = r − j.
A unique maximal term in an ultrametric sum gives a nonzero sum.
Roots of unity γ_i have absolute value 1 < q^{s_i q/(q−1)}.
acceptance: Li(1) = Σ_d ℓ_d^{−1} has leading term 1.

nodes.statement: For d ≥ 0 and 1 ≤ s ≤ q, S_d(s) = ℓ_d^{−s} (Carlitz). Consequently, for every array (ε; s) with s_i ≤ q for all i and every d ∈ Z, S_d(ε; s) = Si_d(ε; s) and S_{<d}(ε; s) = Si_{<d}(ε; s), hence ζ_A(ε; s) = Li(ε; s); in particular ζ_A(s) = Li(s) for s ∈ I^T_w and for s ∈ I^0_w, and 𝔏^{Li}_d(s) = 𝔏^ζ_d(s), 𝔏^{Li}_{<d}(s) = 𝔏^ζ_{<d}(s) for such s.
proofSteps: The depth-one identity is DM.6/small-power-sum; with characters, both sides acquire the factor ε^d.
Induct on depth using S_d(ε; s) = S_d(ε_1; s_1)S_{<d}(ε_−; s_−) and the same factorisation of Si_d; the tail (ε_−; s_−) again has entries ≤ q.

One has Z_w ⊂ AZ_w and L_w ⊂ AL_w, and each weight space is finite-dimensional because there are 2^{w−1} indices of weight w.

nodes.title: Thakur, small-entry and Hoffman-type index families
nodes.statement: For w ≥ 1: I_w is the set of indices of weight w; Thakur’s family I^T_w = J_w = {s ∈ I_w : s_i ≤ q for i < dep(s), s_{dep(s)} < q}; the small-entry family I^0_w = {s ∈ I_w : every s_i < q}; the Hoffman-type family IND_w = J′_w = I′_w = {s ∈ I_w : q ∤ s_i for every i}; I^T_0 = IND_0 = {∅}. For arrays: AT_w = {(ε; s) : s ∈ J_w}, AS_w = {(ε; s) : s ∈ J′_w}, AJ^1_w = {(ε; s) : s ∈ J_w, ε_i = 1 whenever s_i = q}. The block map ι : J′_w → J_w sends (h_1q + r_1, …, h_nq + r_n), 0 < r_i < q, to (q^{{h_1}}, r_1, …, q^{{h_n}}, r_n), and ϕ : AS_w → AJ^1_w does the same on arrays, placing ε_i over r_i and 1 over the inserted entries q. In weight 0 all these sets are {∅}, resp. {(∅; ∅)}.
proofSteps: ι is a weight-preserving bijection: an element of J_w parses uniquely into blocks, each a run of q’s ending in an entry < q, and each block (q^{{h}}, r) comes from the entry hq + r.
ϕ is a bijection by the same parsing, the characters riding on the entries r_i.

nodes.title: Carlitz’s evaluation of ζ_A(q − 1)
nodes.statement: With π̃ = 1/Ω(θ) the Carlitz period of DM.2 and D_1 = θ^q − θ, ζ_A(q − 1) = Li(q − 1) = −π̃^{q−1}/D_1. The right side does not depend on the chosen (q − 1)-th root of −θ, since π̃^{q−1} ∈ K_∞ (DM.2/period-power). More generally z/e_C(z) = 1 + Σ_{m ≥ 1, (q−1) | m} ζ_A(m)(z/π̃)^m near z = 0.
hypotheses: e_C the Carlitz exponential with kernel π̃A (DM.2).
proofSteps: By DM.2/lattice-exponential applied to the lattice π̃A (DM.2/carlitz-period), e_C(z) = z∏_{0 ≠ a ∈ A}(1 − z/(aπ̃)).
e_C is F_q-linear with derivative 1, so the logarithmic derivative gives 1/e_C(z) = 1/z + Σ_{a ≠ 0} 1/(z − aπ̃) = 1/z − Σ_{n ≥ 1} z^{n−1} Σ_{a ≠ 0}(aπ̃)^{−n}.

Writing a = cb with c ∈ F_q^× and b monic, Σ_{a ≠ 0} a^{−n} = (Σ_{c ∈ F_q^×} c^{−n}) ζ_A(n), and Σ_{c} c^{−n} is −1 if (q − 1) | n and 0 otherwise (Mathlib FiniteField.sum_pow_units); this gives the generating identity.
Since e_C(z) = z + z^q/D_1 + O(z^{q²}), z/e_C(z) = 1 − z^{q−1}/D_1 + O(z^{2(q−1)}); comparing the coefficient of z^{q−1} gives ζ_A(q − 1)/π̃^{q−1} = −1/D_1.
ζ_A(q − 1) = Li(q − 1) by MZ.0/carlitz-identity, since q − 1 ≤ q.
acceptance: For q = 2, ζ_A(1) = −π̃/(θ² + θ), and for q = 3, ζ_A(2) = −π̃²/(θ³ − θ); both were checked in the Laurent expansion in 1/θ against π̃^{q−1} = −θ^q∏_{i ≥ 1}(1 − θ^{1−q^i})^{−(q−1)}.

nodes.title: Eulerian values
nodes.statement: An element z ∈ C_∞ is Eulerian of weight w ≥ 1 if z ∈ K·π̃^w; this is independent of the choice of the period, which changes by a factor in F_q^× (DM.2/carlitz-period). Since v_∞(π̃) = −q/(q − 1), the valuation of π̃^w is an integer iff (q − 1) | w. Hence, if (q − 1) ∤ w, no nonzero element of C_const := ⋃_{n ≥ 1} F_{q^n}((1/θ)) ⊂ C_∞ (which contains K_∞) has the form cπ̃^w with c ∈ F̄_q(θ); in particular a nonzero element of K_∞ is never Eulerian of weight w. (With coefficients c ∈ K̄ the analogue fails: (−θ)^{−w/(q−1)}π̃^w lies in K_∞.)
hypotheses: π̃ from DM.2; v_∞ extended to C_∞.
proofSteps: |π̃|_∞ = q^{q/(q−1)} (DM.2/carlitz-period), so v_∞(π̃^w) = −wq/(q − 1), an integer iff (q − 1) | wq iff (q − 1) | w, as gcd(q, q − 1) = 1.
Elements of F̄_q(θ)^× and of C_const^× have integer valuations, so cπ̃^w ∈ C_const with c ≠ 0 forces v_∞(π̃^w) ∈ Z.
π̃ ∈ ρ·K_∞^× with ρ^{q−1} = −θ (from the product formula of DM.2/carlitz-period), which shows that the restriction on the coefficient field cannot be dropped.
C_const denotes the union of the finite constant-field Laurent series fields; no identification with the full Laurent series field over F̄_q is needed.
acceptance: ζ_A(q − 1) is Eulerian of weight q − 1; for q = 2 every weight is divisible by q − 1.

Δ^{[j]}_{a,b} = Δ^{[j]}_{b,a}, and Δ^{[j]}_{a,b} = 0 for all j when a + b ≤ q.
hypotheses: q = p^e; the coefficients are reduced modulo p.
proofSteps: Symmetry is visible from the formula.

If a + b ≤ q, the only j < a + b divisible by q − 1 is j = q − 1 with a + b = q; then binom(q − 2, a − 1) = binom(q − 2, b − 1) and the signs (−1)^{a−1}, (−1)^{b−1} are opposite when q is odd (a + b = q odd), while for q even 2 = 0; so the coefficient vanishes.

nodes.title: Chen’s equal-degree product formula
nodes.statement: For positive integers a, b and every d ∈ Z, S_d(a)S_d(b) = S_d(a + b) + Σ_{0<j<a+b} Δ^{[j]}_{a,b} S_d(a + b − j, j). With characters, S_d(ε; a)S_d(ε′; b) = S_d(εε′; a + b) + Σ_j Δ^{[j]}_{a,b} S_d(εε′, 1; a + b − j, j) (Harada). In particular S_d(a)S_d(b) = S_d(a + b) when a + b ≤ q.
proofSteps: For d < 0 both sides vanish; for d = 0 there are no off-diagonal pairs and the depth-two sums vanish.
For d ≥ 1 write S_d(a)S_d(b) as a sum over pairs (u, v) of monic degree-d polynomials; the diagonal u = v gives S_d(a + b).

For u ≠ v set h = u − v, so 0 ≠ h has degree < d and both (u, h) and (v, h) parametrise the off-diagonal pairs; partial fractions give 1/(u^a v^b) = Σ_{m=1}^{a} (−1)^b binom(a + b − m − 1, b − 1)/(u^m h^{a+b−m}) + Σ_{m=1}^{b} (−1)^{b−m} binom(a + b − m − 1, a − 1)/(v^m h^{a+b−m}), an integer identity valid in every characteristic.

Every nonzero h of degree < d is uniquely cg with c ∈ F_q^× and g monic, so Σ_{0 ≠ h, deg h < d} h^{−j} = −S_{<d}(j) when (q − 1) | j and 0 otherwise (Mathlib FiniteField.sum_pow_units). nodes.title: The index space with its harmonic and q-shuffle products
nodes.statement: H = ⊕_{w ≥ 0} H_w is the K-vector space with basis the set I of indices (including ∅), graded by weight, with [s] the basis element of s and Supp(P) the indices with nonzero coefficient. The multilinear bracket [P_1, …, P_ℓ] extends concatenation (so [s, 0] = 0 while [s, ∅] = [s]). The box-plus map ⊞ : H × H → H is bilinear with ∅ ⊞ P = P ⊞ ∅ = 0 and s ⊞ n = (s_+, s_r + n_1, n_−). The harmonic product ∗ = ∗^{Li} is the bilinear map with [∅] ∗ P = P ∗ [∅] = P and [s] ∗ [n] = [s_1, s_− ∗ n] + [n_1, s ∗ n_−] + [s_1 + n_1, s_− ∗ n_−]; the q-shuffle product ∗^ζ has the same unit and recursion plus the correction D^ζ_{s,n} = Σ_{j=1}^{s_1+n_1−1} Δ^{[j]}_{s_1,n_1}[s_1 + n_1 − j, (j) ∗^ζ (s_− ∗^ζ n_−)] (D^{Li} := 0). Both products are commutative, preserve weight, and every u ∈ Supp(s ∗^• n) has max(dep s, dep n) ≤ dep u ≤ dep s + dep n.
hypotheses: Coefficients in K; Δ from MZ.1/chen-coefficient.
proofSteps: Both products are defined by recursion on dep(s) + dep(n); the correction term only calls products of smaller total depth.
Weight homogeneity and the depth bounds follow by induction on dep(s) + dep(n) (Chang–Chen–Mishiba Proposition A.1.1, Corollary A.1.2).
Commutativity follows from the symmetry of the recursion and of Δ^{[j]}_{a,b}.
If s_1 + n_1 ≤ q then D^ζ_{s,n} = 0, so the two products agree on indices with all entries summing below q at each step.

nodes.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ}, all P, Q ∈ H, all positive-depth indices s, n and every d ∈ Z: 𝔏^•(P)𝔏^•(Q) = 𝔏^•(P ∗^• Q); 𝔏^•_{<d}(P)𝔏^•_{<d}(Q) = 𝔏^•_{<d}(P ∗^• Q); and 𝔏^•_d(s)𝔏^•_d(n) = 𝔏^•_d([s_1 + n_1, s_− ∗^• n_−]) + 𝔏^•_d(D^•_{s,n}). Thus ∗ realises the stuffle relations of CMPL values and ∗^ζ realises Thakur’s q-shuffle relations of MZVs.
hypotheses: Products and realisations from MZ.1/index-algebra and MZ.1/realisation-maps.
proofSteps: The fixed-degree formula reduces to depth one: for • = Li, ℓ_d^{−s_1}ℓ_d^{−n_1} = ℓ_d^{−(s_1+n_1)}; for • = ζ, MZ.1/chen-product.

The truncated formula is proved by induction on d, splitting 𝔏^•_{<d}(s)𝔏^•_{<d}(n) according to which leading degree is larger, using the fixed formula for equal leading degrees and the induction hypothesis for the tails.

nodes.title: Controlled product expansions of power sums
nodes.statement: For arrays (ε; s), (ε′; t) there are finitely many coefficients and arrays, independent of d, such that for every d ∈ Z: (1) S_d(ε; s)S_d(ε′; t) = Σ f_i S_d(μ_i; u_i), (2) S_{<d}(ε; s)S_{<d}(ε′; t) = Σ f′_i S_{<d}(μ′_i; u′_i), (3) S_d(ε; s)S_{<d}(ε′; t) = Σ f″_i S_d(μ″_i; u″_i), with coefficients in F_p for indices (trivial characters; Thakur, Ngo Dac) and in F_q for arrays (as Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham state; the same induction gives F_p), every array ≤ (ε; s) + (ε′; t) in the preorder of MZ.0/index (so of the same character and weight) and of depth ≤ dep(s) + dep(t); the same holds for Si in place of S, where the expansion is the stuffle expansion. For trivial characters and nonempty a, the mixed expansion has the form S_d(a)S_{<d}(b) = Σ f″_i S_d(a_1, c_i) with c_i ≤ a_− + b.
hypotheses: Arrays of positive depth; characters in F_q^×.
proofSteps: Induct on dep(s) + dep(t) as in Thakur 2010 Theorem 3 (with the corrected induction) and Ngo Dac Proposition 2.1: the base case is MZ.1/chen-product (for S) or the identity Si_d(ε; s)Si_d(ε′; t) = Si_d(εε′; s + t) (for Si). The author’s correction, credited to Shuhui Shi (source issue E23), proves the mixed identity first at each depth, then the equal-degree identity; use that order.
For (1) factor off the leading entries and expand the tails by (2); for (2) split by the larger leading degree; (3) follows from (2).
Each step preserves character and weight and keeps the prefix sums dominated, using the calculus of MZ.0/index.

nodes.title: Binary relations between power sums
nodes.statement: Fix a realisation (Thakur power sums S_d, or Carlitz power sums Si_d, of arrays). A binary relation of weight w is a pair of finitely supported K-coefficient families (a_i) on arrays (ε_i; s_i) and (b_j) on arrays (ε′_j; t_j), all of weight w, such that Σ_i a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ_j b_j S_{d+1}(ε′_j; t_j) = 0 for every d ∈ Z; it is fixed when every b_j = 0. They form a K-vector space BR_w. In the formal setting of MZ.1, P^• = {(P, Q) ∈ H ⊕ H : 𝔏^•_d(P) + 𝔏^•_{d+1}(Q) = 0 for all d ∈ Z} and P^•_w = P^• ∩ (H_w ⊕ H_w), both entries homogeneous of weight w. Summing over d, a binary relation gives the linear relation Σ a_i ζ_A(ε_i; s_i) + Σ b_j ζ_A(ε′_j; t_j) = 0 (resp. with Li, resp. 𝔏^•(P) + 𝔏^•(Q) = 0).
hypotheses: Coefficients in K; the identity is required for every integer d, including negative d.
proofSteps: BR_w and P^•_w are subspaces since the defining identities are linear.
Summation: Σ_{d ∈ Z}(Σ a_i S_d + Σ b_j S_{d+1}) = Σ a_i ζ_A(ε_i; s_i) + Σ b_j ζ_A(ε′_j; t_j), the shift d ↦ d + 1 being harmless over all of Z (Ngo Dac Remark 2.4).

nodes.title: Thakur’s fundamental relation R_1
nodes.statement: For every d ∈ Z, S_d(q) + D_1 S_{d+1}(1, q − 1) = 0 and Si_d(q) + D_1 Si_{d+1}(1, q − 1) = 0, where D_1 = θ^q − θ = −ℓ_1; with characters, Si_d(ε; q) + ε^{−1}D_1 Si_{d+1}(ε, 1; 1, q − 1) = 0 (the relation R_ε), and the same for S. Hence ζ_A(q) + D_1 ζ_A(1, q − 1) = 0 = Li(q) + D_1 Li(1, q − 1).
proofSteps: For d < 0 both terms vanish. For d ≥ 0, Si_{d+1}(1, q − 1) = ℓ_{d+1}^{−1}Σ_{j=0}^{d}ℓ_j^{1−q}, and one proves Σ_{j=0}^{d}ℓ_j^{1−q} = −(θ − θ^{q^{d+1}})/(D_1 ℓ_d^{q−1}) by induction on d: for d = 0 both sides are 1, and the inductive step reduces to −(θ − θ^{q^{d+1}})^q + θ^q − θ = θ^{q^{d+2}} − θ.
Since ℓ_{d+1} = ℓ_d(θ − θ^{q^{d+1}}), this gives D_1 Si_{d+1}(1, q − 1) = −ℓ_d^{−q} = −Si_d(q).
The S version follows by MZ.0/carlitz-identity, all entries being ≤ q; the character version multiplies both terms by ε^d.

nodes.title: Todd’s operators B*, C and the cancellation operator BC
nodes.statement: Let R be a binary relation of weight w, R(d): Σ a_i S_d(ε_i; s_i) + Σ b_j S_{d+1}(ε′_j; t_j) = 0. For an array (σ; v) of depth one, B*_{σ,v}(R) is the fixed relation of weight w + v obtained from S_d(σ; v)·Σ_{e<d}R(e), namely Σ a_i S_d(σ, ε_i; v, s_i) + Σ b_j S_d(σ, ε′_j; v, t_j) + Σ b_j S_d(σ; v)S_d(ε′_j; t_j) = 0, the last product expanded by MZ.1/power-sum-products; B*_{Σ,V} = B*_{σ_1,v_1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ B*_{σ_n,v_n} (B*_0 is not defined). For an array (Σ; V) of weight v, C_{Σ,V}(R) is the binary relation of weight w + v obtained from R(d)·S_{<d+1}(Σ; V). For ε ∈ F_q^×, BC_{ε,q}(R) = B*_{ε,q}(R) − Σ_j b_j C_{ε′_j,t_j}(R_ε), whose equal-degree terms cancel, leaving Σ a_i S_d(ε, ε_i; q, s_i) + Σ b_{jk} S_{d+1}(ε, ε″_{jk}; 1, t_{jk}) = 0 with (ε″_{jk}; t_{jk}) ≤ (1; q − 1) + (ε′_j; t_j). In the formal setting the same operators B^•_s, C^•_s and BC^{•,m}_q (m-fold iterate, BC^{•,m}_q(P, Q) = ([q^{{m}}, P], L_1^m α^{•,m}_q(Q))) act on H_{>0} ⊕ H_{>0}.
hypotheses: Binary relations from MZ.2/binary-relation; expansions from MZ.1/power-sum-products.
proofSteps: B*: multiply Σ_{e<d}R(e) = Σ a_i S_{<d}(ε_i; s_i) + Σ b_j (S_{<d} + S_d)(ε′_j; t_j) by S_d(σ; v) and use S_d(σ; v)S_{<d}(x) = S_d(σ, x).
C: multiply R(d) by S_{<d+1}(Σ; V) = S_{<d}(Σ; V) + S_d(Σ; V) and expand by MZ.1/power-sum-products; coefficients stay in K, only the structure constants lie in F_p.

BC: by definition of C on R_ε, the terms S_d(ε, ε′_j; q, t_j) + S_d(ε; q)S_d(ε′_j; t_j) of B*_{ε,q}(R) cancel; what remains is the fixed part and the shifted part −Σ b_j ε^{−1}D_1 S_{d+1}(ε; 1)S_{<d+1}(1; q − 1)S_{<d+1}(ε′_j; t_j).

Small heads: if v + (t_j)_1 ≤ q for every j then S_d(σ; v)S_d(ε′_j; t_j) = S_d(σε′_{j1}; v + t_{j1}, …), and if R is fixed then B*_{σ,v} only prepends (σ; v) (Ngo Dac Corollaries 2.6–2.7; Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham Lemmas 1.5 and 4.4).
Each operator sends binary relations to binary relations of the shifted weight (Chang–Chen–Mishiba Proposition A.3.1).
acceptance: B*_{q}(R_1) followed by subtraction of C_{(1,q−1)}(R_1) is BC_q(R_1), whose fixed part is S_d(q, q).

nodes.title: The controlled form of C_W(R_1)
nodes.statement: For a nonempty index W = (w_1, W_−), C_W(R_1) has the form S_d(q + w_1, W_−) + Σ_i a_i S_d(s_i) + Σ_i b_i S_{d+1}(1, t_i) = 0 with a_i, b_i ∈ K, s_i ≤ (q) + W and (s_i)_1 < q + w_1, and t_i ≤ (q − 1) + W. For arrays (Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham Proposition 1.6), C_{Σ,V}(R_ε) = Si_d(εσ_1, Σ_−; q + v_1, V_−) + Si_d(ε, Σ; q, V) + Σ_i b_i Si_{d+1}(ε, ε_i; 1, t_i) with b_i ∈ A divisible by D_1 and (ε_i; t_i) ≤ (1; q − 1) + (Σ; V).
hypotheses: W, (Σ; V) nonempty; R_1, R_ε from MZ.2/fundamental-relation.
proofSteps: By the definition of C, C_W(R_1) is S_d(q, W) + S_d(q)S_d(W) + D_1 S_{d+1}(1)S_{<d+1}(q − 1)S_{<d+1}(W) = 0.

Expand S_d(q)S_d(W) by MZ.1/power-sum-products: the leading term is S_d(q + w_1, W_−), the others have first entry < q + w_1 and are ≤ (q) + W; the term S_d(q, W) also joins the a_iS_d(s_i), since (q, W) ≤ (q) + W and its first entry is q < q + w_1.
Expand S_{<d+1}(q − 1)S_{<d+1}(W) by MZ.1/power-sum-products into S_{<d+1}(t_i) with t_i ≤ (q − 1) + W, and absorb S_{d+1}(1).
For Si the product Si_d(ε; q)Si_d(Σ; V) is exactly Si_d(εσ_1, Σ_−; q + v_1, V_−), so no further terms appear, and the shifted coefficients are ε^{−1}D_1 times F_q-structure constants, hence in D_1A.
acceptance: For W = (1), C_{(1)}(R_1) has leading term S_d(q + 1).

nodes.title: The reduction step for a bad index
nodes.statement: (1) Let s = (s_1, …, s_r) with s_1, …, s_{k−1} ≤ q and s_k > q. Then ζ_A(s) = Σ a_i ζ_A(s′_i) + Σ b_i ζ_A(t′_i) + Σ c_i ζ_A(u_i) with a_i, b_i, c_i ∈ K, every index t on the right has dep(t) ≥ dep(s) and T_k(t) ≤ T_k(s), and: type 1 indices have Init(s′) ≻ Init(s), or Init(s′) = Init(s) and s′_k < s_k; type 2 indices have t′_1 + ⋯ + t′_ℓ < s_1 + ⋯ + s_ℓ for k ≤ ℓ ≤ dep(s); type 3 indices have Init(u) ≻ Init(s). (2) If every entry of s is ≤ q and s_k = q is the last entry (k = r), the same holds with only types 2 (prefix sums up to k strictly smaller) and 3. (3) For arrays and the Si (Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham Proposition 1.7(1)), with any chosen ε ∈ F_q^×: Li(ε; s) = −Li(ε′; s′) + Σ b_i Li(ε′_i; t′_i) + Σ c_i Li(μ_i; u_i), with b_i, c_i ∈ A divisible by D_1 and the single type-1 array (ε′; s′) = (ε_1, …, ε_{k−1}, ε, ε^{−1}ε_k, ε_{k+1}, …; s_1, …, s_{k−1}, q, s_k − q, s_{k+1}, …); every array on the right has depth ≥ dep(s) and T_k ≤ T_k(s), the type-1 and type-2 arrays have prefix sums strictly smaller than those of s at every length ℓ with k ≤ ℓ ≤ dep(s), and type-3 arrays have Init(u) ≻ Init(s). When Init(s) = s and the last entry is q (Proposition 1.7(2)) there is no type-1 term. (4) For the S of arrays (Proposition 4.6) the same holds except that type 1 is a K-combination Σ a_i ζ_A(ε′_i; s′_i) with Init(s′_i) ≽ Init(s) and (s′_i)_k < s_k, all coefficients lying in K.
hypotheses: s_k > q in case (1); s_k = q terminal in case (2).
proofSteps: Put W = (s_k − q, s_{k+1}, …, s_r) and start from C_W(R_1) (MZ.2/c-of-fundamental), whose leading term is S_d(s_k, …, s_r); for (3) start from C_{Σ,V}(R_ε) with the chosen ε, whose second term is the type-1 array.
Let j < k be maximal with s_j < q (s_0 := 0), so s_{j+1} = ⋯ = s_{k−1} = q; apply BC_q k − j − 1 times, controlling the shifted indices by t ≤ (q^{{k−j−1}}, s_k − 1, s_{k+1}, …).
If j ≥ 1 apply B*_{s_j} (small-head rule, as s_j < q) and then B*_{s_1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ B*_{s_{j−1}} (fixed relations); if j = 0 skip B*_{s_j} and sum the relation directly (source issue E2), then sum over d.
The three families of terms are the three types; their properties follow from the support bounds of MZ.1/power-sum-products and the dominance calculus of MZ.0/index.
For (2) use W = ∅ (C_∅(R_1) = R_1); for (3) run the same construction with R_ε and the chosen ε, noting that the C-terms of Si carry no extra fixed terms and that every coefficient stays in D_1A.
acceptance: For s = (q + 1), the reduction gives ζ_A(q + 1) as a combination of ζ_A(q, 1) (type 1) and indices (1, t) of depth ≥ 2 (type 2).

nodes.title: Reduction to k-admissible indices
nodes.statement: For every k ≥ 1 and every index s, ζ_A(s) is a K-linear combination of ζ_A(t) with t k-admissible, wt(t) = wt(s), dep(t) ≥ dep(s) and T_k(t) ≤ T_k(s). The same holds for Li(ε; s) and for ζ_A(ε; s) in terms of k-admissible arrays of the same weight. The reduction terminates: at fixed weight and fixed k, each step strictly decreases (s_1 + ⋯ + s_k; reverse lexicographic rank of Init(s) in the finite set of initial tuples of weight ≤ w; the entry after Init(s)) in the lexicographic order.
proofSteps: For ζ_A(s), induct on k; for the array versions the cited statements give only “same weight, k-admissible”, the depth and T_k bounds holding by the same proof. For k = 1: if s_1 ≤ q then s is 1-admissible or s = (q), handled by R_1; if s_1 > q use C_{(s_1 − q, s_2, …)}(R_1) and induct on s_1.
For k ≥ 2 assume the statement for k − 1, so s may be taken (k − 1)-admissible but not k-admissible, hence dep(s) ≥ k; induct on s_1 + ⋯ + s_k.
Apply MZ.2/reduction-step (case (1) or (2)); type 2 terms have smaller s_1 + ⋯ + s_k and are handled by induction; terms with equal sum are of type 1 or 3, with Init weakly increasing.
Init(s) ≼ q^{{k}} lies in a finite set, so Init eventually stabilises; then only type 1 steps occur and the entry after Init strictly decreases, which cannot continue forever.
acceptance: k = w applied to an index of weight w gives indices in I^T_w (MZ.0/index).

nodes.title: Brown’s theorem in positive characteristic
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1, the family {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} spans Z_w over K; hence dim_K Z_w ≤ d(w) (Ngo Dac’s Theorem A). Likewise AT_w spans AL_w (the weak Brown theorem for ACMPLs), {ζ_A(ε; s) : (ε; s) ∈ AT_w} spans AZ_w, and {Li(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} spans L_w (trivial characters). The proof gives an algorithm expressing every value as such a combination.
proofSteps: Apply MZ.2/admissible-reduction with k = w; a w-admissible index of weight w lies in I^T_w (MZ.0/index).
|I^T_w| = d(w) by MZ.0/counting.

The alternating and CMPL versions are the same argument with the array forms of the reduction step; the CMPL version is the trivial-character specialisation of the ACMPL one, the operators preserving characters.
acceptance: For q = 2 the algorithm gives ζ_A(3) = (θ² + θ)²(ζ_A(1, 1, 1) + ζ_A(2, 1)) (checked in the Laurent expansion).
For w ≤ q, I^T_w = IND_w is the set of compositions of w other than (q), and the theorem reduces to R_1.

sources.match: States that every MZV of weight w is a K-combination of elements of T_w, so dim_K Z_w ≤ d(w), and deduces it from Proposition 3.2 with k = w.
States the weak Brown theorems for ACMPLs and AMZVs with the generating set AT_w.

nodes.title: The bridge between zeta values and polylogarithm values
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 0, AZ_w = AL_w and Z_w = L_w.
proofSteps: By MZ.2/brown-spanning, AZ_w is spanned by the AMZVs of AT_w and AL_w by the ACMPLs of AT_w.
Arrays of AT_w have all entries ≤ q, so their AMZV and ACMPL agree (MZ.0/carlitz-identity).
Restricting to trivial characters gives Z_w = L_w from the CMPL version of the weak Brown theorem (source issue E10 for the use of this specialisation).

Shows {𝔏^•(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} generates Z^•_w for both realisations, so Z^{Li}_w = Z^ζ_w.

nodes.title: The Thakur decomposition and the rewriting operator U^•
nodes.statement: Every index has a unique decomposition s = (s^T, q^{{m}}, s′) with s^T ∈ I^T (Thakur’s family of any weight, or ∅), m ≥ 0, and s′ = ∅ or s′_1 > q; put Init(s) = (s^T, q^{{m}}) and, if s′ ≠ ∅, s″ = (s′_1 − q, s′_−). For • ∈ {Li, ζ} let α^•_q(P) = [1, (q − 1) ∗^• P] with iterates α^{•,m}_q (α^{•,0}_q = id). The K-linear map U^• : H → H is U^•(s) = −[s^T, q^{{m+1}}, s″] + L_1^{m+1}[s^T, α^{•,m+1}_q(s″)] + L_1^{m+1}(s^T ⊞ α^{•,m+1}_q(s″)) − [s^T, q^{{m}}, D^•_{q,s″}] if s′ ≠ ∅, and U^•(s) = L_1^m[s^T, α^{•,m}_q(∅)] + L_1^m(s^T ⊞ α^{•,m}_q(∅)) if s′ = ∅, with L_1 = θ − θ^q. Write U^• = U^•_1 + U^•_2 + U^•_3 for the bracket terms, the ⊞ term and the correction term. U^• preserves weight and fixes every index of I^T.
proofSteps: The decomposition is unique: (s^T, q^{{m}}) is Ngo Dac’s Init(s), and s^T is Init(s) with its maximal terminal run of q’s removed, m being the length of that run.
Each component is a finite combination of indices of the weight of s (Chang–Chen–Mishiba Remark 3.2.3).

nodes.title: The rewriting theorem
nodes.statement: For • ∈ {Li, ζ} and every P ∈ H: (1) 𝔏^•(U^•(P)) = 𝔏^•(P); (2) there is an explicit e ≥ 0 with Supp((U^•)^e(P)) ⊂ I^T. Consequently {𝔏^•(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} spans Z^•_w = 𝔏^•(H_w), and Z^{Li}_w = Z^ζ_w = Z_w.
proofSteps: (1): for s ∉ I^T with s′ ≠ ∅, the relation BC^{•,m}_q(C^•_{s″}(R_1)), followed by B^•_{s^T} when s^T ≠ ∅, lies in P^•_{wt(s)} by MZ.2/todd-operators, and its realisation reads 𝔏^•(s) − 𝔏^•(U^•(s)) = 0 (Chang–Chen–Mishiba (A.3.3)–(A.3.4)); for s′ = ∅ (then m ≥ 1) use BC^{•,m−1}_q(R_1) ((A.3.5)–(A.3.6)).

(2): for s ∉ I^T every n ∈ Supp(U^•(s)) has dep(n) > dep(s) (component U_1), or dep(n) = dep(s) and Init(n) > Init(s) (U_2), or dep(n) = dep(s), Init(n) ≥ Init(s) and n_{ℓ+1} < s_{ℓ+1} with ℓ = dep Init(s) (U_3) (Lemma A.3.7).
The triple (dep; Init; −entry after Init) lives in a finite totally ordered set at fixed weight, so the iteration stops (Theorem A.3.8).
Ngo Dac’s spanning theorem is recovered, simultaneously for both realisations, together with Z^{Li}_w = Z^ζ_w from MZ.0/carlitz-identity on I^T.

nodes.title: The Hoffman-type generating set
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1, Z_w is spanned by the values Li(s) with s ∈ IND_w.
proofSteps: Choose e ≫ 0 with (U^{Li})^e(H_w) ⊂ span I^T_w over F_p[L_1] (MZ.2/rewriting-theorem), and let U = (u_{s,n}) ∈ Mat_{d(w)}(F_p[L_1]) with (U^{Li})^e(s) = Σ_{n ∈ I^T_w} u_{s,n}[n] for s ∈ IND_w.
For s = (m_1q + n_1, …, m_rq + n_r) ∈ IND_w, D^{Li} = 0 gives U^{Li}(s) ≡ −[s^T, q, s″] modulo L_1, so (U^{Li})^e(s) ≡ (−1)^{m_1+⋯+m_r}[ι(s)] modulo L_1.
ι is a bijection (MZ.0/index-families), so det U ≡ ±1 modulo L_1 and det U ≠ 0; hence the Li(s), s ∈ IND_w, span the same space as the ζ_A(n), n ∈ I^T_w, which is Z_w by MZ.2/rewriting-theorem.
acceptance: For w ≤ q, IND_w = I^T_w and the statement is MZ.2/rewriting-theorem.

nodes.title: The strong Brown theorem for alternating polylogarithms
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1, the ACMPL values Li(ε; s) with (ε; s) ∈ AS_w span AL_w; hence dim_K AL_w ≤ s(w). More precisely, for each (ε; s) ∈ AT_w let (ε′; s′) ∈ AS_w be its contraction: parse s into blocks, each a run of q’s ending in an entry < q, replace the i-th block (q^{{h_i − 1}}, r_i) by the single entry (h_i − 1)q + r_i (so ι(s′) = s), and let ε′_i be the product of the characters of the i-th block. Then Li(ε′; s′) = Σ_{(ϵ; t) ∈ AT_w} a^{(ε;s)}_{ϵ,t} Li(ϵ; t) with every a ∈ A, a ≡ ±1 modulo D_1 for (ϵ; t) = (ε; s) and a ≡ 0 modulo D_1 otherwise. The contraction is many-to-one onto AS_w, and the t(w) × t(w) matrix (a^{(ε;s)}_{ϵ,t}), with rows indexed by AT_w (repeated left-hand sides allowed), is invertible.
proofSteps: Fix (ε; s) ∈ AT_w and run the reduction algorithm of MZ.2/admissible-reduction with k = w on its contraction (ε′; s′), using MZ.2/reduction-step (3) at every step, also at the first step in place of C(R_1).
Every coefficient is −1 on a type-1 edge and lies in D_1A otherwise, so the coefficient of a leaf is congruent modulo D_1 to the product along its all-type-1 path.

Splitting the m-th q off the i-th entry of s′, choose the free character in the reduction step equal to the character of the corresponding entry of (ε; s); the all-type-1 chain then ends at (ε; s) with sign (−1)^{n−ℓ}, and every other leaf of AT_w is reached through a non-type-1 edge.

This gives the congruences for every row; the t(w) × t(w) matrix is congruent modulo D_1 to a diagonal matrix with entries ±1, so its determinant is not divisible by D_1 and the matrix is invertible over K.

Inverting it expresses every Li(ϵ; t), (ϵ; t) ∈ AT_w, as a K-combination of the Li(ε′; s′), which lie in AS_w; with the weak Brown theorem (MZ.2/brown-spanning: AT_w spans AL_w), AS_w spans AL_w. The bijection ϕ is only used for |AS_w| = s(w) (MZ.0/counting). Source issue E9 records that the published proof cites Propositions 1.7 and 1.10 without this bookkeeping, and E21 that it writes AJ_w for the index set of AT_w.
acceptance: For w ≤ q, AS_w = AT_w and the statement is the weak Brown theorem; for q = 2 the two sets differ but have the same cardinality d(w).

sources.match: States that AS_w generates AL_w and proves it by a transition matrix that is ±1 on the diagonal modulo D_1.

nodes.title: The next-weight relation ζ_A(2q − 1) + D_1 ζ_A(1, 2q − 2) = 0
nodes.statement: For every prime power q and every d ∈ Z, S_d(2q − 1) + D_1 S_{d+1}(1, 2q − 2) = 0; hence ζ_A(2q − 1) + D_1 ζ_A(1, 2q − 2) = 0. For q > 2 both indices lie in IND_{2q−1}, so the MZVs indexed by IND_w are not independent at w = 2q − 1.
proofSteps: Expand C_{(q−1)}(R_1) = S_d(q, q − 1) + S_d(q)S_d(q − 1) + D_1 S_{d+1}(1)S_{<d+1}(q − 1)² = 0. By MZ.1/chen-product, Δ^{[q−1]}_{q,q−1} = −1 and Δ^{[2q−2]}_{q,q−1} = 0, so S_d(q)S_d(q − 1) = S_d(2q − 1) − S_d(q, q − 1), which cancels the first term.

S_{<d+1}(q − 1)² = 2S_{<d+1}(q − 1, q − 1) + Σ_{i ≤ d}S_i(q − 1)², and S_i(q − 1)² = S_i(2q − 2) + 2(−1)^q S_i(q − 1, q − 1) (Δ^{[q−1]}_{q−1,q−1} = 2(−1)^q); the coefficient 2(1 + (−1)^q) of S_{<d+1}(q − 1, q − 1) vanishes in characteristic p, so S_{<d+1}(q − 1)² = S_{<d+1}(2q − 2) and C_{(q−1)}(R_1) is the claimed relation.
Equivalently, this is the case n = 0, s_1 = s_2 = 1, k_1 = 0 of Lara Rodríguez–Thakur Theorem 3.1(2): ζ(1, 2q − 2) = ζ(2q − 1)/ℓ_1, with ℓ_1 = −D_1.
For q > 2, neither 2q − 1 nor 2q − 2 is divisible by q.
acceptance: Checked numerically for q = 2 and q = 3 in the Laurent expansion.

Gives ζ(a, b) = ζ(a + b)/ℓ_1^{s_1 q^n} for the stated families, which contains (a, b) = (1, 2q − 2).
Recalls that ζ_A(1, 2q − 2) and ζ_A(2q − 1) are dependent.

nodes.title: Anderson–Thakur polynomials and Carlitz factorials
nodes.statement: Let [k] = θ^{q^k} − θ and D_k = ∏_{ℓ=1}^{k}[ℓ]^{q^{k−ℓ}} (D_0 = 1; this is DM.0’s D_k = ∏_{j<k}(θ^{q^k} − θ^{q^j})). For n ≥ 1 write n − 1 = Σ_j n_j q^j in base q and put Γ_n = ∏_j D_j^{n_j} (the Carlitz factorial of n − 1). Let γ_0(t) = 1 and γ_j(t) = ∏_{ℓ=1}^{j}(θ^{q^j} − t^{q^ℓ}). The Anderson–Thakur polynomials α_n(t) ∈ A[t] are defined by Σ_{n ≥ 1} α_n(t)x^n/Γ_n = x(1 − Σ_{j ≥ 0} γ_j(t)x^{q^j}/D_j)^{−1}, and H_n(t) ∈ A[t] is α_n with θ and t interchanged. (In Anderson–Thakur and Chang the same polynomial is called H_{n−1}; this roadmap uses Ngo Dac’s and Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham’s indexing.) Then deg_θ H_n ≤ (n − 1)q/(q − 1) < nq/(q − 1), so ‖H_n‖ < |θ|^{nq/(q−1)}; H_n = 1 for 1 ≤ n ≤ q; and H_{q+k−1} = (t^q − t) + (k − 1)(t^q − θ^q) for 1 < k ≤ q − 1.
proofSteps: Expanding the geometric series, the coefficient of x^n for n ≤ q comes only from the j = 0 term, so α_n/Γ_n = 1 and Γ_n = 1, whence H_n = 1.

For n = q + k − 1 with 1 < k ≤ q − 1 exactly one factor γ_1 x^q/D_1 can occur, in k − 1 positions, so α_n/Γ_n = 1 + (k − 1)γ_1/D_1 with Γ_n = D_1; hence α_n = (θ^q − θ) + (k − 1)(θ^q − t^q) and H_n follows by swapping θ and t.
The degree bound is Anderson–Thakur’s estimate (3.7.3), as quoted by Ngo Dac §4.2, Chang Theorem 5.5.1 and Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham (2.4).

sources.match: Defines [k], D_k, Γ_n through the digits of n − 1, γ_j, α_n by the generating series and H_n by swapping θ and t, with the Gauss-norm bound and the index shift relative to the cited sources.

nodes.title: Anderson–Thakur interpolation of power sums
nodes.statement: For s ≥ 1 and d ≥ 0, (H_s Ω^s)^{(d)}(θ) = Γ_s S_d(s)/π̃^s, where f^{(d)} raises coefficients to the q^d-th power (DM.8/coefficient-twist) and Ω, π̃ = 1/Ω(θ) are as in DM.2. With a character, if γ ∈ F̄_q satisfies γ^{q−1} = ε, then (γH_sΩ^s)^{(d)}(θ) = γε^d Γ_s S_d(s)/π̃^s.
hypotheses: s ≥ 1, d ≥ 0; H_s in Ngo Dac’s indexing.
proofSteps: This is Anderson–Thakur’s interpolation formula (Anderson–Thakur 1990, (3.7.3)–(3.7.4); Anderson–Thakur 2009, 2.4.1), as stated in Chang 2014 Theorem 5.5.1; its proof expresses S_d(s) through the coefficients of the Carlitz exponential and the polynomials γ_j. The original proof was not reread here (the Annals paper is not freely available); this is recorded as a gap.
The character version follows from γ^{q^d} = γε^d (MZ.0/carlitz-multiple-polylogarithm).
acceptance: For s ≤ q, H_s = 1 and Γ_s = 1, and the formula reads Ω^{(d)}(θ)^s = S_d(s)/π̃^s, i.e. ℓ_d^{−s}π̃^{−s} = S_d(s)π̃^{−s}, which is Carlitz’s identity, since Ω^{(d)} = Ω/𝕃_d with 𝕃_d(θ) = ℓ_d.

nodes.title: Chang’s deformation series
nodes.statement: Let 𝕃_0(t) = 1 and 𝕃_d(t) = ∏_{i=1}^{d}(t − θ^{q^i}), so 𝕃_d(θ) = ℓ_d and Ω^{(d)} = Ω/𝕃_d. For an index s of depth r ≥ 1 and Q = (Q_1, …, Q_r) ∈ K̄[t]^r with the termwise bound ‖Q_j‖ < |θ|^{q s_j/(q−1)} for every j (Gauss norm), Chang’s series is 𝔏(s; Q) = Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0}(Ω^{s_r}Q_r)^{(d_r)}⋯(Ω^{s_1}Q_1)^{(d_1)} = Ω^{wt(s)}Σ_{d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0}Q_r^{(d_r)}⋯Q_1^{(d_1)}/(𝕃_{d_r}^{s_r}⋯𝕃_{d_1}^{s_1}), with 𝔏(∅) = 1. Special cases: Q = (H_{s_1}, …, H_{s_r}) gives Ngo Dac’s L(s); Q = (γ_1H_{s_1}, …) with γ_i^{q−1} = ε_i gives 𝔏(s; ε); Q = (γ_1, …, γ_r) gives 𝔏𝔦(s; ε); Q = (1, …, 1) gives Chang–Chen–Mishiba’s 𝓛(s). The termwise bound holds for every consecutive sub-tuple, so every series 𝔏(s_j, …, s_k; Q_j, …, Q_k) is defined.
hypotheses: Q_j ∈ K̄[t] with the termwise bound (source issue E8: the whole-tuple condition printed by Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham does not suffice).
proofSteps: Ω^{(−1)} = (t − θ)Ω gives Ω^{(1)} = Ω/(t − θ^q) and inductively Ω^{(d)} = Ω/𝕃_d, whence the second expression.

The twist raises the absolute values of coefficients to the q^d-th power, so ‖f^{(d)}‖ = ‖f‖^{q^d} for the Gauss norm, and ‖Ω‖ = |ρ|^{−q} = |θ|^{−q/(q−1)} since every factor 1 − t/θ^{q^i} has Gauss norm 1.

Under the termwise bound the general term has Gauss norm ∏_j c_j^{q^{d_j}} with c_j = ‖Q_j‖/|θ|^{q s_j/(q−1)} < 1, so the series converges in the Tate algebra T of DM.8, for the tuple and for each consecutive sub-tuple.
‖H_n‖ < |θ|^{nq/(q−1)} (MZ.3/anderson-thakur-polynomials) and |γ| = 1 show that the four special cases satisfy the bound.

nodes.title: Entireness of Chang’s series
nodes.statement: Under the termwise bound, 𝔏(s; Q) lies in the ring E of DM.8: its coefficients are algebraic over K, generate a finite extension of K_∞, and the series converges on all of C_∞. The same holds for every consecutive sub-tuple. More generally, if every Q_j is nonzero and the whole-tuple decay condition of Chang Lemma 5.3.1 holds, the series for the tuple and every initial sub-tuple are entire; no claim about arbitrary tails is made under that weaker condition.
hypotheses: Either the termwise bound; or, for the initial-sub-tuple assertion only, Q_j ≠ 0 and ∏_j (‖Q_j‖/|θ|^{q s_j/(q−1)})^{q^{d_j}} → 0 as d_1 > ⋯ > d_r ≥ 0 and d_1 → ∞.
proofSteps: By MZ.3/deformation-series, 𝔏(s; Q) and the series of all its consecutive sub-tuples lie in T, and Ω ∈ T (DM.2/omega).

The vector ψ = (Ω^{s_1+⋯+s_r}, 𝔏(s_1; Q_1)Ω^{s_2+⋯+s_r}, …, 𝔏(s_1, …, s_{r−1}; …)Ω^{s_r}, 𝔏(s; Q))^T has entries in T and, by the twist recursion of MZ.3/deformation-series, satisfies ψ^{(−1)} = Φψ for the lower bidiagonal Φ ∈ Mat_{r+1}(K̄[t]) with diagonal (t − θ)^{s_{k+1}+⋯+s_r} and subdiagonal Q_k^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{s_k+⋯+s_r}; det Φ is a power of t − θ, so det Φ(0) ≠ 0.

DM.8/entire-from-equation (Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas Proposition 3.1.3) gives ψ ∈ E^{r+1}: every entry is entire with algebraic coefficients generating a finite extension of K_∞; in particular Ω ∈ E and 𝔏(s; Q) ∈ E. Sub-tuples are treated the same way (Chang’s proof of Lemma 5.3.1 follows this route).

For the weaker whole-tuple condition put c_j = ‖Q_j‖/|θ|^{q s_j/(q−1)} > 0. To test a prefix of length k, shift all its summation indices by r−k and append the fixed indices r−k−1, …, 0. The whole-tuple norm is a fixed positive constant times the q^{r−k}-th power of the prefix norm. Thus decay for the whole tuple implies decay for every prefix. This puts the displayed first-column vector in T, and the same equation and DM.8/entire-from-equation put it in E; convergence of the other columns is unnecessary (Chang Lemma 5.3.1, proof, p. 15).

nodes.statement: (1) For j ≥ 0, 𝔏(s; Q)(θ^{q^j}) = 𝔏(s; Q)(θ)^{q^j}. (2) At t = θ: 𝔏(s; H)(θ) = Γ_s ζ_A(s)/π̃^{wt(s)} with Γ_s = Γ_{s_1}⋯Γ_{s_r}; 𝔏(s; ε)(θ) = γ_1⋯γ_r Γ_s ζ_A(ε; s)/π̃^{wt(s)}; 𝔏𝔦(s; ε)(θ) = γ_1⋯γ_r Li(ε; s)/π̃^{wt(s)}; 𝓛(s)(θ) = Li(s)/π̃^{wt(s)}.

nodes.title: The dual t-motives attached to an index
nodes.statement: For (s; Q) as in MZ.3/deformation-series, Φ_{s,Q} ∈ Mat_{r+1}(K̄[t]) is the lower bidiagonal matrix with diagonal entries (t − θ)^{s_{k+1}+⋯+s_r} (k = 0, …, r; the last is 1) and subdiagonal entries Q_k^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{s_k+⋯+s_r} (k = 1, …, r). Ψ_{s,Q} ∈ GL_{r+1}(T) is lower triangular with (k, j)-entry 𝔏(s_{j+1}, …, s_k; Q_{j+1}, …, Q_k)Ω^{s_{k+1}+⋯+s_r} for j ≤ k (the empty series being 1), so the diagonal is Ω^{s_{k+1}+⋯+s_r} and the last row is (𝔏(s; Q), 𝔏(s_2, …; Q_2, …), …, 𝔏(s_r; Q_r), 1). Then Ψ_{s,Q}^{(−1)} = Φ_{s,Q}Ψ_{s,Q}, all entries of Ψ lie in E, and det Φ_{s,Q} = (t − θ)^{Σ_{k=0}^{r−1}(s_{k+1}+⋯+s_r)}. The K̄[t]-module M_{s,Q} = K̄[t]^{r+1} with σ acting by Φ_{s,Q} is an effective dual t-motive (DM.4) and Ψ_{s,Q} is a rigid analytic trivialisation; M′_{s,Q} is given by the upper-left r × r block, with trivialisation the upper-left block of Ψ.
hypotheses: Termwise bound on Q; K̄ perfect, so the effective dual t-motive of DM.4 is defined.
proofSteps: Twisting by −1 lowers every summation index by one; separating the terms whose last index becomes −1 gives 𝔏(s_{j+1}, …, s_k)^{(−1)} = 𝔏(s_{j+1}, …, s_k) + Q_k^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{s_k}Ω^{s_k}𝔏(s_{j+1}, …, s_{k−1}); with Ω^{(−1)} = (t − θ)Ω this is the (k, j) entry of Ψ^{(−1)} = ΦΨ.
det Φ is the product of the diagonal entries, a power of t − θ; so (t − θ)^N kills M/σM and M is an effective dual t-motive.
Ψ is lower triangular with unit-multiple diagonal entries Ω^{…} ∈ T^×, hence invertible over T; its entries lie in E by MZ.3/deformation-entire.

nodes.title: Chang’s MZ property
nodes.statement: A nonzero Z ∈ C_∞ has the MZ property of weight w ≥ 1 if there are d ≥ 2, Φ ∈ Mat_d(K̄[t]) and ψ ∈ E^d with ψ^{(−1)} = Φψ such that: (1) det Φ = c(t − θ)^m with c ∈ K̄^× and m ≥ 0; (2) the last column of Φ is (0, …, 0, 1)^T; (3) ψ(θ) has first entry π̃^{−w} and last entry cZ/π̃^w for some c ∈ K^×; (4) for every N ≥ 1, every entry of ψ(θ^{q^N}) except the last vanishes, and the last is (cZ/π̃^w)^{q^N}.
hypotheses: E, the twist and the ABP condition from DM.8; π̃ from DM.2.
proofSteps: The data (Φ, ψ) is a witness; the weight is determined by Z (a consequence of MZ.3/chang-descent).
Products: if Z_i have the MZ property of weight w_i, Kronecker products of the witnesses give the MZ property of weight Σ m_iw_i for Z_1^{m_1}⋯Z_n^{m_n} (Chang Proposition 3.4.4).

nodes.title: Chang’s descent theorem and the graded algebra of values
nodes.statement: Let w_1, …, w_ℓ be distinct positive integers and V_i a finite set of MZ-property values of weight w_i, each V_i K-linearly independent. Then {1} ∪ V_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ V_ℓ is K̄-linearly independent. Moreover, if Z_1, …, Z_n have the MZ property of the same weight w and π̃^w, Z_1, …, Z_n are K̄-linearly dependent, they are K-linearly dependent. Consequences: (a) MZ-property values of one weight are K-independent iff K̄-independent (Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham Proposition 2.3); (b) the K̄-algebra 𝒵 generated by all MZVs is graded, 𝒵 = K̄ ⊕ ⊕_{w ≥ 1}𝒵_w, and defined over K (K̄ ⊗_K Z → 𝒵 is bijective), and the same holds for CMPL values at algebraic points (Chang Theorems 2.2.1 and 5.4.3); (c) if ζ_A(s)/π̃^{wt(s)} ∈ K̄ then it lies in K.
proofSteps: Step I (separation of the top weight w_1 > ⋯): form the block-diagonal system with blocks (t − θ)^{w_1 − w_i}Φ_{ij} and vectors Ω^{w_1 − w_i}ψ_{ij} (entries in E, since Ω ∈ E by MZ.3/deformation-entire); apply ABP lifting (DM.8/abp-lifting) to a relation, normalise, and specialise at θ^{q^N}, where the lower-weight blocks vanish, to get a K̄-relation inside V_1.

Step II (descent from K̄ to K in one weight): lift a K̄-relation by ABP, divide by the last coordinate, compare the twisted and untwisted lifts; the coefficients become σ-invariant rational functions, hence lie in F_q(t) (DM.8/analytic-fixed-fields), and specialising gives a K-relation, contradicting the hypothesis.
The same argument with the extra entry 1 in place of a weight-w block gives the statement with π̃^w (Chang Proposition 4.3.1).
(b) follows by Chang Theorem 5.5.2 (ζ_A(s) = Γ_s^{−1}Σ_u a_u Li_s(u) with u in a finite set of algebraic points) and MZ.3/mz-property-values; (c) is the case n = 1 of the statement with π̃^w.
acceptance: (a) applied to I^T_w and the basis theorem gives that I^T_w is a K̄-basis of 𝒵_w (Chang–Chen–Mishiba Remark 1.2.6).

nodes.title: The merged prefix system of a putative relation
nodes.statement: Fix w ≥ 1, finitely many pairs (s_i; Q_i), i = 1, …, n, with wt(s_i) = w and Q_i ∈ K̄[t]^{dep(s_i)} satisfying the termwise bound, and coefficients a, a_1, …, a_n ∈ A, with a_i(t) = a_i|_{θ=t} ∈ F_q[t]. Let I be the set of proper prefixes (t; Q) of the pairs, including ∅. Define Φ′ ∈ Mat_{|I|}(K̄[t]) by Φ′_{∅,∅} = (t − θ)^w, Φ′_{(t;Q),(t;Q)} = (t − θ)^{w−wt(t)}, Φ′_{(t;Q),(t′;Q′)} = Q_{last}^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{w−wt(t′)} when (t′; Q′) is (t; Q) with its last entry removed, and 0 otherwise; the row v with v_{(t;Q)} = Σ_i a_i(t)Q_{i,last}^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{w−wt(t)} over the i whose penultimate prefix is (t; Q); and Φ = [[Φ′, 0], [v, 1]]. Define Ψ′ by Ψ′_{∅,∅} = Ω^w and Ψ′_{(t;Q),(t′;Q′)} = 𝔏(t after t′; Q after Q′)Ω^{w−wt(t)} when (t′; Q′) is a prefix of (t; Q), 0 otherwise; the row f with f_{(t;Q)} = Σ_i a_i(t)𝔏(s_i after t; Q_i after Q) over the i having (t; Q) as a proper prefix; and Ψ = [[Ψ′, 0], [f, 1]]. Finally Φ̃ = diag(1, Φ) and ψ̃ = (1, (Ψ′_{(t;Q),∅})_{(t;Q) ∈ I}, f_∅)^T. Then Ψ^{(−1)} = ΦΨ, Ψ ∈ GL_{|I|+1}(T) with entries in E, det Φ = (t − θ)^{Σ_{(t;Q) ∈ I}(w − wt(t))}, ψ̃^{(−1)} = Φ̃ψ̃, ψ̃ ∈ E^{|I|+2}, and the last coordinate of ψ̃(θ) is Σ_i a_i𝔏(s_i; Q_i)(θ).

proofSteps: Each block of Φ′, Ψ′ restricted to the prefixes of one pair is Φ′_{s_i,Q_i}, Ψ′_{s_i,Q_i} of MZ.3/index-dual-motive, so the equation Ψ′^{(−1)} = Φ′Ψ′ holds blockwise, and the merged rows agree because a prefix determines its own entries.
The last row: f^{(−1)} = vΨ′ + f is the defining recursion of the suffix series, as in MZ.3/index-dual-motive.
Φ′ is lower triangular for the order by length, with diagonal powers of t − θ; Ψ′ is lower triangular with diagonal Ω^{w−wt(t)} ∈ T^×.
Entries of Ψ lie in E by MZ.3/deformation-entire; the value of f_∅ at θ is Σ a_i𝔏(s_i; Q_i)(θ) by definition.
acceptance: For one pair s = (1, q − 1), Q = 1, the system has I = {∅, (1)} and is the system of Chang–Chen–Mishiba Example 4.3.2 before solving.

nodes.title: The ABP independence criterion for zeta-type periods
nodes.statement: In the setting of MZ.3/prefix-system, assume (LW) for each weight w′ < w the values 𝔏(t; Q)(θ), (t; Q) ∈ I of weight w′, are K-linearly independent (in particular nonzero), and (LD) a + Σ_i a_i𝔏(s_i; Q_i)(θ) = 0 with a, a_i ∈ A not all zero. Then: there are b ∈ F_q[t] ∖ {0} and δ_0, δ_{(t;Q)} ∈ K̄[t] with δ_0^{(−1)} = δ_0 and [[Id, 0], [δ, 1]]^{(−1)}[[Φ′, 0], [bv, 1]] = [[Φ′, 0], [0, 1]][[Id, 0], [δ, 1]] (δ = (δ_{(t;Q)})); there is ν ∈ F_q[t]^{|I|} with δΨ′ + bf = ν; and for every (t; Q) ∈ I, f_{(t;Q)}(θ) = ν_{(t;Q)}(θ)/b(θ) ∈ K. For Ngo Dac’s case (Q = H, a = 0) and Chang–Chen–Mishiba’s case (Q = 1, Σ a_s Li(s) = cπ̃^w, so a = −c after clearing π̃) this is the rationality step of their proofs. Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham state the setup with constant tuples Q_i (source issue E11); the proof uses only the Frobenius specialisation, the descent of MZ.3/chang-descent and the DM.8 inputs, so it applies to every Q with the termwise bound, which is this roadmap’s formulation.
hypotheses: (LW) and (LD) as stated; the termwise bound on all Q_i.
proofSteps: Apply ABP lifting (DM.8/abp-lifting) to (Φ̃, ψ̃) and ρ = (a, 0, …, 0, 1): det Φ̃ is a power of t − θ with constant 1, and ρψ̃(θ) = 0 by (LD); get a polynomial row h with hψ̃ = 0 and h(θ) = ρ, and put g = h/h_last, regular at θ.
B = g − g^{(−1)}Φ̃ has last entry 0 and Bψ̃ = gψ̃ − (gψ̃)^{(−1)} = 0, i.e. B_0 + Σ B_{(t;Q)}𝔏(t; Q)Ω^{w−wt(t)} = 0.

Specialise at θ^{q^j}, j ≫ 0, where Ω vanishes: B_0 = 0; dividing by Ω^{w−w_0} for the largest prefix weight w_0 and specialising gives a K̄-relation among the 𝔏(t; Q)(θ)^{q^j} of weight w_0, which is trivial by (LW) and MZ.3/chang-descent (a); so those B vanish, and descending through the weights all B vanish.

Then the unipotent gauge equation holds; by DM.8/constant-denominator the common denominator b of the entries lies in F_q[t]; with δ = b·(entries), X = [[Id, 0], [δ, 1]][[Ψ′, 0], [bf, 1]] satisfies X^{(−1)} = diag(Φ′, 1)X, so by uniqueness of rigid trivialisations (the API item fundamental_unique of DM.8/fundamental-matrix: every solution is Ψ times a constant matrix) X = diag(Ψ′, 1)[[Id, 0], [ν, 1]] with ν over F_q(t); δΨ′ + bf = ν lies in T, so ν ∈ F_q[t] (DM.8/analytic-fixed-fields).

Specialise δΨ′ + bf = ν at θ^{q^j}: δΨ′ vanishes there, and b, ν, a_i are fixed by twisting, so the Frobenius specialisation of MZ.3/deformation-specialisation gives b(θ)^{q^j}f(θ)^{q^j} = ν(θ)^{q^j}; take q^j-th roots (source issue E19: Ngo Dac cites (4.2) where (5.4) is needed).
acceptance: For the two indices (w) and (k, q − 1) with Q = H and a = 0 the gauge equation is Ngo Dac’s two-row system (6.3)–(6.4) (MZ.4/two-row-system).

nodes.title: The Eulerian suffix constraint
nodes.statement: Under the conclusion of MZ.3/independence-criterion: (1) if (q − 1) ∤ w and the 𝔏-values come from ACMPL or CMPL periods, then a = 0. (2) For CMPL values (Q = 1) and a nonempty proper prefix s ∈ 𝔦(M): Σ_{s′} a_{(s,s′)}Li(s′) ∈ K·π̃^{w−wt(s)}, so either Σ_{s′} a_{(s,s′)}Li(s′) = 0 or (q − 1) | (w − wt(s)); if for every nonempty prefix the suffix values Li(s′), (s, s′) ∈ Supp, are K-independent, then every index in the support has (q − 1) | s_2, …, s_r. (3) For MZVs (Q = H), every nonempty proper prefix t gives Σ_i a_iΓ_{suffix_i}ζ_A(suffix_i) ∈ K·π̃^{w−wt(t)}, with i ranging over its support and Γ_{suffix_i} the product of the suffix factorials. If these suffix values are K-independent then the sum is nonzero and (q − 1) | (w − wt(t)). In particular, after discarding zero coefficients, if t belongs to exactly one s_i, then ζ_A(s_i after t)/π̃^{w−wt(t)} ∈ K, and (q − 1) divides the suffix weight; for indices in I^0_w this forces every entry of s_i after the first position not shared with another index to equal q − 1.
hypotheses: The setting and conclusion of MZ.3/independence-criterion.
Every index called part of the support has nonzero coefficient; repeated indices are collected first.
proofSteps: f_{(s;1)}(θ) = Σ_{s′} α_{(s,s′)}(θ)𝓛(s′)(θ) = Σ_{s′}a_{(s,s′)}Li(s′)/π̃^{w−wt(s)} lies in K by the criterion and MZ.3/deformation-specialisation.
A nonzero element of K_∞ that is Eulerian of weight w − wt(s) forces (q − 1) | (w − wt(s)) (MZ.0/eulerian); the support statement follows when the suffix values are independent.
For (1): the constant a corresponds to aπ̃^w, and a nonzero a would make π̃^w a combination of elements of C_const = ⋃_n F_{q^n}((1/θ)), impossible for (q − 1) ∤ w by MZ.0/eulerian.

For (3), the period specialisation gives f_t(θ) = (Σ_i a_iΓ_{suffix_i}ζ_A(suffix_i))/π̃^{w−wt(t)} ∈ K. Each factorial is nonzero, so independence of the suffixes makes its numerator nonzero. For an isolated tail this is automatic from nonvanishing. Successive isolated tails, when all entries are < q, force each later entry to equal q − 1.
acceptance: For q = 2 every weight is divisible by q − 1 and the constraint is empty.

sources.match: Proves that each suffix combination is Eulerian of the suffix weight and deduces the support condition (q − 1) | s_2, …, s_r.
Deduces from rationality that isolated tails are Eulerian and that later entries of small-entry indices equal q − 1, and the divisibility of suffix weights for q-indivisible indices.

nodes.title: The Frobenius difference systems (E_M) and their solution spaces
nodes.statement: Let R = {f/g : f ∈ K̄[t], 0 ≠ g ∈ F_q[t]} ⊂ K̄(t), an F_q(t)-algebra stable under the coefficient twist f ↦ f^{(1)} (which fixes F_q(t)). For an index s let 𝔦(s) = {∅, (s_1), (s_1, s_2), …, s} and for a set M let 𝔦(M) = ∪_{s ∈ M}𝔦(s). For w ≥ 0 and ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w, the system (E_M) for (ε_s)_{s ∈ 𝔦(M)} ∈ R^{𝔦(M)} is ε_s^{(1)} = (ε_s + Σ ε_{(s,n)})(t − θ)^{w−wt(s)} for s ∈ 𝔦(M), the sum over positive integers n with (s, n) ∈ 𝔦(M). Let IND°_0 = {∅} and, for w > 0, IND°_w = {s ∈ IND_w : (q − 1) | s_2, …, s_{dep(s)}}; (E_w) is (E_M) for M = IND°_w, and X_w ⊂ R^{𝔦(IND°_w)} is its set of solutions, an F_q(t)-vector space. For arrays of a fixed character ε with γ^{q−1} = ε, the twisted system of Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham asks for δ_{(t;ε)} ∈ K̄[t] with δ_{(t;ε)} = (δ_{(t;ε)} + Σ δ_{child})^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{w−wt(t)} at nonempty prefixes and with the children terms multiplied by γ^{(−1)} at ∅, δ at a full index being its coefficient a_i(t).
hypotheses: w ≥ 0; M a nonempty finite set of weight-w indices.
proofSteps: R is stable under twisting because g^{(1)} = g for g ∈ F_q[t]; F_q(t)-linear combinations of solutions are solutions since the twist fixes F_q(t).
For s ∈ M the equation reads ε_s^{(1)} = ε_s, so ε_s ∈ F_q(t) (DM.8/analytic-fixed-fields).
acceptance: (E_0) is ε_∅^{(1)} = ε_∅ and X_0 = F_q(t); for w = q, IND°_q = {(1, q − 1)} and (E_q) has three equations; for q ≥ 3 and w = 2q − 2, IND°_w = {(q − 1, q − 1), (2q − 2)} and (E_w) has four equations.

nodes.title: Monic Frobenius descent
nodes.statement: Let F = Σ_{i=0}^{n} f_i t^i and G be in A[t], with n = deg_t F ≥ 1 and f_n ∈ F_q^×. If ε ∈ R satisfies ε^{(1)} = εF + G, then ε ∈ F_q(t)[θ]; if ε ∈ K̄[t], then ε ∈ A[t]. More generally, if a subring B of a field of characteristic p is stable under q-th powers, F ∈ B[t] is monic of positive degree, G ∈ B[t], and a polynomial δ over the field satisfies δ^{(1)} = Fδ + G, then δ ∈ B[t]. The twisted variant: if εδ = δ^{(−1)}(t − θ)^m + F^{(−1)} with ε ∈ F_q^×, m ≥ 1, δ ∈ K̄[t] and F ∈ F_q[t, θ] (resp. F̄_q[t, θ]), then δ ∈ F_q[t, θ] (resp. F̄_q[t, θ]); the proof uses ε^q = ε.
hypotheses: deg_t F ≥ 1 is essential; for a general subring B the twist f ↦ f^{(1)} is the coefficientwise q-th power map, which needs no perfectness.
proofSteps: Multiply ε by a common denominator g ∈ F_q[t] (g^{(1)} = g) to assume ε ∈ K̄[t] of t-degree m; then G has t-degree m + n.

Comparing coefficients of t^i for i = m + n, m + n − 1, …: the top coefficients give a_{i−n}f_n = −g_i − Σ_{j > i−n}a_jf_{i−j}, which determines a_m, a_{m−1}, … successively in A; once i ≤ m the extra term a_i^q appears but involves an already determined coefficient, so every coefficient lies in A (Chang–Chen–Mishiba Lemma 4.2.2).
The general and twisted versions are the same descending induction (Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham Lemma 3.3, after Kuan–Lin).
Positive degree matters: over B = F_2, F = 1 and G = 1, a root δ ∈ F_4 of δ² − δ = 1 solves δ^{(1)} = δ + 1 without lying in F_2.
acceptance: Applied to Ngo Dac’s equation δ_2^{(1)} = (t − θ^q)^{q−1}(δ_2 + a_2) it puts δ_2 in A[t] (source issue E6).

sources.match: Proves that a solution in R of ε^{(1)} = εF + G with F monic up to F_q^× of positive t-degree lies in F_q(t)[θ], by descending coefficient comparison.
Proves the twisted variant with a character ε and F ∈ F_q[t, θ] or F̄_q[t, θ], after Kuan–Lin.
Cites Kuan–Lin for δ_1, δ_2 ∈ K[t]; the needed membership in A[t] follows from this lemma (source issue E6).

nodes.title: The θ-degree bound for solutions
nodes.statement: If (ε_s) ∈ R^{𝔦(M)} solves (E_M) (w ≥ 0, ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w), then ε_s ∈ F_q(t)[θ] and deg_θ ε_s ≤ (w − wt(s))/(q − 1) for every s ∈ 𝔦(M). In the twisted form, a solution δ ∈ F_q[t, θ] of εδ = δ^{(−1)}(t − θ)^m + F^{(−1)} has deg_θ δ ≤ max{qm/(q − 1), deg_θ F/q}.
proofSteps: Induct on w − wt(s). For s ∈ M, ε_s ∈ F_q(t). Otherwise the children ε_{(s,n)} lie in F_q(t)[θ] by induction; after multiplying the equation by a common denominator g ∈ F_q[t] of ε_s and of the children (g^{(1)} = g), MZ.4/monic-frobenius-descent applies with F = (t − θ)^{w−wt(s)} and G = g(t − θ)^{w−wt(s)}Σε_{(s,n)} ∈ A[t], so ε_s ∈ F_q(t)[θ].
If deg_θ ε_s exceeded (w − wt(s))/(q − 1), then deg_θ ε_s^{(1)} = q deg_θ ε_s would exceed both deg_θ(ε_s(t − θ)^{w−wt(s)}) and the degrees of the other terms (bounded by induction), a contradiction.
The twisted bound is the same comparison of θ-degrees after twisting once.
acceptance: For s ∈ M the bound gives deg_θ ε_s ≤ 0, consistent with ε_s ∈ F_q(t).

sources.match: Proves ε_s ∈ F_q(t)[θ] and deg_θ ε_s ≤ (w − wt(s))/(q − 1) for solutions of (E_M).
Proves deg_θ δ ≤ max{qm/(q − 1), deg_θ F/q}.

nodes.title: The key lemma: relations give solutions of (E_M)
nodes.statement: Let w ≥ 0, ∅ ≠ M ⊂ I_w and P = Σ a_s[s] ∈ H with a_s ∈ K and Supp(P) ⊂ M. Suppose Li_P(1) = Σ a_s Li(s) ∈ K·π̃^w and, for each 0 ≤ ℓ < w, the values Li(s), s ∈ 𝔦(M) ∩ I_ℓ, are K-linearly independent. Then (1) for each s ∈ 𝔦(M), Σ_{s′} a_{(s,s′)}Li(s′) = 0 or (q − 1) | (w − wt(s)) (MZ.3/eulerian-tails); and (2) (E_M) has a solution (ε_s) ∈ F_q(t)[θ]^{𝔦(M)} with ε_s = a_s|_{θ=t} for every s ∈ M.
hypotheses: Coefficients a_s cleared to lie in A (so a_s|_{θ=t} ∈ F_q[t]); w > 0 for (2) to be non-trivial.
proofSteps: Apply MZ.3/independence-criterion to the pairs (s; 1), s ∈ M, with a = −c where Li_P(1) = cπ̃^w; its hypotheses are the assumptions.

The gauge equation [[Id, 0], [g, 1]]^{(−1)}[[Φ′, 0], [v, 1]] = [[Φ′, 0], [0, 1]][[Id, 0], [g, 1]] has rational entries with denominator in F_q[t] (DM.8/constant-denominator); put ε_s = g_s^{(−1)} for s ∈ 𝔦(M) ∖ M and ε_s = a_s|_{θ=t} for s ∈ M.
Reading the gauge equation row by row gives exactly (E_M); MZ.4/theta-degree-bound puts the solution in F_q(t)[θ].

sources.match: Proves both parts: the Eulerian alternative for each prefix, and a solution of (E_M) in F_q(t)[θ] with ε_s = a_s|_{θ=t} on M.

nodes.title: The dimension of the solution space X_w
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 0, dim_{F_q(t)}X_w = 1 if (q − 1) | w and 0 otherwise. When w = ℓ(q − 1), a generator (η_{ℓ;s}) can be chosen with η_{ℓ;∅} = Σ_{i=0}^{ℓ}b_{ℓi}(t − θ)^i, b_{ℓℓ} = 1 and b_{ℓi} ∈ T·F_p[T]_{(T)} for i < ℓ, where T = t − t^q and F_p[T]_{(T)} is the localisation at (T).
proofSteps: By MZ.4/theta-degree-bound, X_w ⊂ F_q(t)[θ]^{𝔦(IND°_w)} with deg_θ ε_∅ ≤ ℓ when w = ℓ(q − 1) + s′, 0 ≤ s′ < q − 1.
The equations at nonempty prefixes (ℓ − j)(q − 1) [+ s′] are copies of (E_{j(q−1)}), so by induction on ℓ the children of ∅ are f_j·(normalised generators of lower weight), f_j ∈ F_q(t).

Write ε_∅ = Σ a_i(t − θ)^i and substitute into the root equation; using t − θ^q = T + (t − θ)^q with T = t − t^q and comparing coefficients of (t − θ)^ν for ν = iq (i < ℓ − m) and ν ≥ w gives a square (or one-larger) linear system U(a, f)^T = a_ℓ b over F_p[T]_{(T)}. In the divisible case there are 2ℓ − m unknowns and equations (source issue E22 corrects the matrix size printed in point (iii)).

det(U mod T) = ±1 by the explicit block structure (identity, then −Id_n and m blocks −Id_{q−1} with inserted unit rows), so U is invertible over the local ring: the solution is unique up to the free parameter a_ℓ when (q − 1) | w, and zero when (q − 1) ∤ w.
acceptance: X_0 = F_q(t); for q = 2 every weight is divisible by q − 1 and X_w is a line; for q = 3 and w = 5, X_5 = 0.

sources.match: Computes dim X_w by induction, reducing to a linear system over F_p[T]_{(T)} whose determinant is ±1 modulo T, with the normalised generator.
