nodes.title: Solutions of the character-twisted system
nodes.statement: In the twisted system of MZ.4/frobenius-system attached to a putative relation a + Σ a_i𝔏𝔦(s_i; ε_i)(θ) = 0 with s_i ∈ J′_w and all ε_i of character ε under the explicit reduced-support hypotheses (q − 1) | s_{i2}, … and ε_i = (ε, 1, …, 1): every solution has, at each nonempty prefix t with m_t = (w − wt(t))/(q − 1), the form δ_t = f_t(X^{m_t} + Σ_{i<m_t}P_{t,i}(T)X^i) with X = t^q − θ^q, T = t − t^q, f_t ∈ F_q[t], P_{t,i} ∈ F_q(y) of y-adic valuation ≥ 1, and the f of children are F_q(T)-multiples of f_t. If (q − 1) ∤ w, or (q − 1) | w and ε ≠ 1, the only solution is zero; if (q − 1) | w and ε = 1, any two polynomial solutions are proportional over F_q(t). Thus their span in the localised ambient space has dimension at most one; existence of a nonzero solution for an arbitrary chosen support is not asserted.
hypotheses: Finite support of distinct weight-w arrays with q dividing none of their entries, later entries divisible by q − 1, and characters (ε, 1, …, 1); b = 1 after clearing a common denominator.
proofSteps: Induct on m_t: at leaves δ = a_i(t) ∈ F_q[t]; at an inner prefix, MZ.4/monic-frobenius-descent and MZ.4/theta-degree-bound give δ_t ∈ K[t] of θ-degree ≤ m_tq and divisible by (t − θ)^{(q−1)m_t}; write δ_t = F(t − θ)^{(q−1)m_t} with deg_θ F ≤ m_t. Since F(t − θ)^{(q−1)m_t} lies in F_q[t, θ^q], F = Σ_{0 ≤ i ≤ m_t/q}f_{m_t−iq}(t − θ)^{m_t−iq} with f ∈ F_q[t], so F(t − θ)^{(q−1)m_t} = Σ f_{m_t−iq}X^{m_t−i} and F^{(1)} = Σ f_{m_t−iq}(T + X)^{m_t−iq}; comparing powers of X gives a linear system with matrix B over F_q(y), y = T, whose diagonal entries are ±1 and whose subdiagonal entries have positive y-adic valuation, whence the stated form.
At the root, with the extra factor γ^{(−1)} = γ/ε: if (q − 1) ∤ w a θ-degree comparison forces deg_θ δ ≤ mq and the same triangular system has only the zero solution.

If (q − 1) | w, comparing the top coefficient gives εf_m = f_m; so ε ≠ 1 forces f_m = 0 and then everything vanishes, while ε = 1 leaves one free parameter. The comparison proves uniqueness up to a rational factor when solutions exist. Multiplying a polynomial solution by an arbitrary element of F_q(t) need not preserve polynomiality, and a smaller support can force the free parameter to vanish.
acceptance: For q = 2 the character is trivial; after ε_t = δ_t^{(−1)} and localising at F_q[t] ∖ {0}, the system on the full reduced support is (E_w). A smaller support is extended by zero.

sources.locator: proof of Theorem 3.4, §3.3 claims 1)–2), Case 1 and Case 2 with its subcases, pp. 37–42
sources.match: Determines the coefficient shape and rational proportionality of solutions on the reduced support, ruling out nonzero solutions at nondivisible weights or nontrivial total character; it does not assert existence on every chosen support.

nodes.title: Ngo Dac’s two-row system in weights q < w ≤ 2q − 2
nodes.statement: Let q > 2, w = q + k − 1 with 2 ≤ k ≤ q − 1 (so q < w ≤ 2q − 2), and let δ_1, δ_2 ∈ K̄[t], a_1, a_2 ∈ F_q[t] satisfy δ_1 = (δ_1 + δ_2H_k + a_1H_w)^{(−1)}(t − θ)^w and δ_2 = (δ_2 + a_2H_{q−1})^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{q−1} (Ngo Dac (6.3)–(6.4)). Then a_2 = 0; for 2 ≤ k < q − 1 also a_1 = 0, while for k = q − 1 the solutions with a_2 = 0 are δ_2 = 0, δ_1 = a(t − θ)^{2q}, a_1 = a(t^q − t) with a ∈ F_q[t] (the Eulerian weight 2q − 2). In particular there is no solution with a_1a_2 ≠ 0. In detail: δ_1, δ_2 ∈ A[t]; δ_2 = f(θ^q − t^q) and a_2 = f(t^q − t) for a unique f ∈ F_q[t]; deg_θ δ_1 ≤ ⌊qw/(q − 1)⌋; and the coefficient comparisons in θ force f = 0.
hypotheses: q > 2; H_k = H_{q−1} = 1 and H_w = (t^q − t) + (k − 1)(t^q − θ^q) (MZ.3/anderson-thakur-polynomials).
proofSteps: Twisting once and MZ.4/monic-frobenius-descent put δ_1, δ_2 in A[t]; a θ-degree comparison bounds deg_θ δ_2 ≤ q and deg_θ δ_1 ≤ ⌊qw/(q − 1)⌋ (source issue E6 replaces the K[t] statement quoted from Kuan–Lin).

Second row: (θ^q − t^q, t^q − t) is a particular solution; the difference Δ = (t^q − t)δ_2 − a_2(θ^q − t^q) satisfies Δ = Δ^{(−1)}(t − θ)^{q−1}, so Δ = 0 by t-degree; evaluating at t = β ∈ F_q shows t^q − t divides a_2, giving the unique f.

First row: δ_1 is divisible by (t − θ)^w, with an integral quotient of θ-degree ≤ 1 (k < q − 1) or ≤ 2 (k = q − 1); write δ_1 = (aθ + b)(t − θ)^w, resp. (aθ² + bθ + c)(t − θ)^w, with a, b, c ∈ F_q[t].
Interior case: comparing the coefficients of θ^k and θ^{k−1} gives a = b = 0, then θ^q gives f = (k − 1)a_1, and finally (t^q − t)a_1 = 0, so a_1 = 0 and f = 0.

Endpoint: the coefficients of θ^{2q−1}, θ^{2q−2} give aθ² + bθ + c = a(t − θ)²; with h = a(t^q − t) − a_1 one obtains h[(t − θ^q)² − (t − θ)^{2q}] = (θ^q − t^q)f(t^q − t); substituting θ = t gives h = 0, and then f = 0, so a_2 = 0 and a_1 = a(t^q − t). Conversely these are solutions, by the identity (t^q − t)[(t^q − t) − 2(t^q − θ^q)] = (t − θ^q)² − (t^q − θ^q)².
Ngo Dac’s argument only needs the absence of solutions with a_2 ≠ 0, since the putative relation involves both indices with nonzero coefficients (MZ.5/q-indivisible-independence).
acceptance: For q = 3, w = 4 (k = 2), take a = 1: a_1 = t³ − t, a_2 = δ_2 = 0 and δ_1 = (t − θ)^6 satisfy both rows. This catches the false assertion that every solution is zero; a_2 ≠ 0 is what the independence proof excludes.

sources.match: Reduces Theorem 6.2 to the two-row system, solves the second row explicitly and derives contradictions from θ-coefficient comparisons in the interior case and at k = q − 1.

nodes.title: Independence of small-entry multiple zeta values
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1 the MZVs ζ_A(s), s ∈ I^0_w (every entry < q), are K-linearly independent, hence K̄-linearly independent; so dim_K Z_w ≥ |I^0_w| = c(w).
proofSteps: Induct on w; for w = 1, ζ_A(1) ≠ 0. A relation with a single index is impossible by MZ.0/mzv-nonvanishing (source issue E16), so assume a relation Σ a_iΓ_{s_i}ζ_A(s_i) = 0, a_i ∈ A ∖ {0}, with at least two indices.

I^0 is closed under taking prefixes (MZ.0/index-families), so by induction and MZ.3/chang-descent the lower-weight prefix values are independent: (LW) holds, and MZ.3/independence-criterion applies with Q = H and a = 0.
By MZ.3/eulerian-tails (3), every entry of s_i after its first unshared position equals q − 1.

Choose two indices with a common prefix of maximal length m; their remaining entries after position m + 1 all equal q − 1 and their weights agree, so their (m + 1)-th entries are congruent modulo q − 1 and lie in [1, q − 1], hence equal, contradicting maximality.
acceptance: For q = 2, I^0_w = {(1, …, 1)} and the theorem says ζ_A(1, …, 1) ≠ 0.

sources.locator: Theorem B, p. 3, and its proof, §5, pp. 18–22; Remark 5.1, p. 22
sources.match: Proves the K-linear independence of the MZVs in T^0_w by induction on the weight through the ABP criterion, rationality of suffix combinations and the longest-common-prefix argument, noting that T^0 is prefix-closed.

nodes.title: Thakur’s basis through weight q
nodes.statement: For 1 ≤ w ≤ q, I^T_w = I^0_w and {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a K-basis of Z_w; dim_K Z_w = d(w).
proofSteps: For w ≤ q, an index of weight w all of whose entries are ≤ q and whose last entry is < q has all entries < q, unless it is (q), which lies in neither family; so I^T_w = I^0_w.
Spanning is MZ.2/brown-spanning and independence MZ.5/small-entry-independence; the count is MZ.0/counting.
acceptance: dim_K Z_1 = 1, dim_K Z_2 = 2 for q > 2, and dim_K Z_q = 2^{q−1} − 1.

sources.match: Deduces from Theorem B that T_w = T^0_w is a basis for w ≤ q, a purely transcendental result since the algebraic part is trivial there.

nodes.title: Independence of q-indivisible MZVs through weight 2q − 2
nodes.statement: For q > 2 and 1 ≤ w ≤ 2q − 2, the MZVs ζ_A(s), s ∈ IND_w, are K-linearly independent.
proofSteps: Induct on w. For w ≤ q, IND_w = I^0_w and MZ.5/small-entry-independence applies (source issue E7: the source writes w < q).

For q < w ≤ 2q − 2, apply strong induction also to the prefixes and suffixes of each supported index, all of which remain q-indivisible and have smaller weight. Prefix independence supplies (LW). For each nonempty proper prefix t, MZ.3/eulerian-tails (3) gives a factorial-weighted suffix combination in K·π̃^{w−wt(t)}; suffix independence and nonzero collected coefficients make this combination nonzero. Thus (q − 1) | (w − wt(t)). Comparing successive prefixes forces every entry after the first to be divisible by q − 1.

With w ≤ 2q − 2 this leaves only (w) and (k, q − 1), k = w − q + 1 ∈ [2, q − 1], so the relation is a_1Γ_wζ_A(w) + a_2ζ_A(k, q − 1) = 0 with a_1, a_2 ≠ 0 (single-index relations being excluded as in MZ.5/small-entry-independence).
Its gauge equation is the two-row system, which has no solution with nonzero a_1, a_2 (MZ.4/two-row-system).
acceptance: At w = 2q − 1 the statement fails: ζ_A(2q − 1) + D_1ζ_A(1, 2q − 2) = 0 (MZ.2/next-weight-relation).

sources.locator: Theorem 6.2 and its proof, pp. 22–24; Remark 6.3, p. 24
sources.match: Proves the independence of T′_w for q > 2 and w ≤ 2q − 2 by the reduction to two indices and the two-row computation, and explains why the method stops at 2q − 1.

nodes.title: Thakur’s basis through weight 2q − 2
nodes.statement: For every prime power q and 1 ≤ w ≤ 2q − 2, {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a K-basis of Z_w, and dim_K Z_w = d(w).
proofSteps: For q = 2, 2q − 2 = q and this is MZ.5/thakur-basis-small-weight.
For q > 2, MZ.5/q-indivisible-independence gives d(w) = |IND_w| independent elements of Z_w, while MZ.2/brown-spanning gives dim_K Z_w ≤ d(w) with I^T_w spanning; so I^T_w is a basis.

sources.locator: Theorem D, p. 4, and its proof, p. 24
sources.match: Deduces the basis property for w ≤ 2q − 2 from Theorem A, Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 6.2.

nodes.title: The CMPL basis indexed by IND_w
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 0, the values Li(s), s ∈ IND_w, form a K-basis of Z_w.
proofSteps: They span Z_w by MZ.2/ind-spanning; it remains to show independence, by induction on w (w = 0 is clear).

Let P = Σ α_s(θ)[s] be a relation supported on IND_w. IND is prefix-closed, so the lower-weight hypothesis of MZ.4/key-lemma holds by induction; part (1) and induction give Supp(P) ⊂ IND°_w, and part (2) with M = IND°_w gives (ε_s) ∈ X_w with ε_s = α_s on IND°_w.
If (q − 1) ∤ w, X_w = 0 (MZ.4/solution-space-dimension), so P = 0.

If (q − 1) | w, π̃^w ∈ Z_w (MZ.1/period-power-in-weight-space), so by MZ.2/ind-spanning there is P_w ≠ 0 supported on IND_w with Li_{P_w}(1) = π̃^w; the key lemma gives Supp(P_w) ⊂ IND°_w and a solution (ε′_s) ∈ X_w; X_w is a line, so (ε_s) = α(ε′_s) and P = α(θ)P_w, whence 0 = Li_P(1) = α(θ)π̃^w and α = 0.
acceptance: For q = 3, IND_4 = {(4), (2, 2), (2, 1, 1), (1, 2, 1), (1, 1, 2), (1, 1, 1, 1)} gives six independent values Li(s) spanning Z_4.

sources.match: Proves that the Li_s(1), s ∈ IND_w, form a basis of Z_w by induction, using Lemma 5.1.1, Theorem 4.3.5 and an element P_w with Li_{P_w}(1) = π̃^w.

nodes.title: Thakur’s basis theorem and Todd’s dimension formula
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1, {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} is a K-basis of Z_w; hence dim_K Z_w = d(w) (Todd’s dimension conjecture, the analogue of Zagier’s conjecture) and Thakur’s basis conjecture (the analogue of Hoffman’s) holds. The same family is a K̄-basis of the K̄-span 𝒵_w of the weight-w MZVs.
proofSteps: {ζ_A(s) : s ∈ I^T_w} spans Z_w (MZ.2/brown-spanning), and dim_K Z_w = |IND_w| = d(w) by MZ.5/cmpl-ind-basis and MZ.0/counting; a spanning family of d(w) elements in a space of dimension d(w) is a basis.
Independently, Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham obtain dim_K Z_w ≥ d(w) from CMPLs (MZ.5/mzv-lower-bound-cmpl) and conclude with Ngo Dac’s spanning theorem.
K̄: the elements have the MZ property of weight w (MZ.3/mz-property-values), so K-independence implies K̄-independence (MZ.3/chang-descent (a)).
acceptance: dim_K Z_w for q = 2 is the Fibonacci number d(w); for q = 3, dim_K Z_5 = d(4) + d(3) + d(2) = 11.

sources.match: Proves Thakur’s basis conjecture and Todd’s dimension conjecture for every w, and notes the K̄-basis statement by Chang’s descent.
Proves the same theorem by the lower bound dim_K Z_w ≥ d(w) and Ngo Dac’s upper bound.

nodes.title: All linear relations among multiple zeta values
nodes.statement: For w ≥ 1 let 𝔏^ζ_w : H_w → Z_w be the realisation and R_w = Span_K{[s] − U^ζ(s) : s ∈ I_w ∖ I^T_w}. Then Ker 𝔏^ζ_w = R_w, and Ker(𝔏^ζ : H → K_∞) = ⊕_{w ≥ 1}R_w. After extension of scalars to K̄, the same relations generate all K̄-linear relations among MZVs.
proofSteps: R_w ⊂ Ker 𝔏^ζ_w by MZ.2/rewriting-theorem (1); since U^ζ fixes I^T, R_w = Span{P − U^ζ(P) : P ∈ H_w}.
With e from MZ.2/rewriting-theorem (2), P ≡ U^ζ(P) ≡ ⋯ ≡ (U^ζ)^e(P) modulo R_w, so H_w/R_w is spanned by the image of I^T_w.
Hence d(w) ≥ dim H_w/R_w ≥ dim H_w/Ker 𝔏^ζ_w = dim Z_w = d(w) (MZ.5/thakur-basis-theorem), forcing Ker 𝔏^ζ_w = R_w.

Across weights, Chang’s grading theorem (MZ.3/chang-descent (b)) shows that a relation among MZVs of mixed weights splits into homogeneous relations, giving ⊕R_w; over K̄ the same argument applies to 𝒵 = K̄ ⊗_K Z.
acceptance: For w = q, R_q contains [q] − L_1[1, q − 1], which is R_1.

sources.match: Proves Ker 𝔏^ζ_w = R_w and Ker 𝔏^ζ = ⊕R_w, the B*-version of Todd’s relation conjecture; the published version adds the K̄ statement as Remark 5.4.

nodes.title: Character splitting of relations among ACMPL periods
nodes.statement: If ε_1, …, ε_n ∈ F_q^× are distinct and γ_i ∈ F̄_q are (q − 1)-th roots of ε_i, then γ_1, …, γ_n are linearly independent over K_∞ = F_q((1/θ)). Consequently, if Σ_i a_i𝔏𝔦(s_i; ε_i)(θ) = 0 with a_i ∈ K and all s_i of weight w, then for each character ε the subsum over the i with χ(ε_i) = ε vanishes.
proofSteps: If ε generates F_q^×, X^{q−1} − ε is irreducible over F_q (a factor of degree d would give γ^{gcd(d, q−1)} ∈ F_q^×, contradicting that ε generates), so 1, γ, …, γ^{q−2} are F_q-independent; every γ_i is an F_q^×-multiple of a power γ^{k_i} with distinct k_i.
F_q(γ) and F_q((1/θ)) are linearly disjoint over F_q (constant field extension), so F_q-independence passes to K_∞-independence.

By MZ.3/deformation-specialisation, 𝔏𝔦(s_i; ε_i)(θ) = γ_{i1}⋯γ_{iℓ_i}Li(ε_i; s_i)/π̃^w, and γ_{i1}⋯γ_{iℓ_i} is a (q − 1)-th root of χ(ε_i); grouping by character and applying the independence of the roots gives the subsums.
acceptance: For q = 3, γ = √−1 and 1 are independent over F_3((1/θ)).

sources.match: Proves that roots of unity attached to distinct characters are independent and that relations among ACMPL periods split by character.

nodes.title: Relations among normalised ACMPL periods
nodes.statement: Let w ≥ 1 and consider K-linear relations a + Σ_i a_i𝔏𝔦(s_i; ε_i)(θ) = 0 with a, a_i ∈ K and s_i ∈ J′_w (no entry divisible by q). They form a K-vector space of dimension at most one, every nonzero relation has a ≠ 0, forces (q − 1) | w, and involves only arrays with trivial character ε_i = (1, …, 1); if (q − 1) | w there is exactly one such relation with a = 1. In particular the ACMPL values Li(ε; s), (ε; s) ∈ AS_w, are K-linearly independent.
proofSteps: Induct on w. For w = 1 and q > 2 use MZ.5/character-splitting and MZ.3/eulerian-tails (1); for q = 2, Li(1) = ζ_A(1) = −π̃/D_1.

Work by strong induction on this relations theorem for the normalised periods, with distinct arrays and nonzero collected coefficients. Character splitting leaves one total character. The absence of homogeneous relations in smaller weight gives (LW) for the prefix periods. For each nonempty prefix, the independence criterion makes its suffix combination a scalar in K; the induction hypothesis applied to that lower-weight relation, including its constant term, forces every supported suffix character to be trivial and its weight divisible by q − 1. Varying the prefix therefore gives later characters 1 and later entries divisible by q − 1. This uses the full induction hypothesis, beyond the valuation conclusion of MZ.3/eulerian-tails; that lemma also gives a = 0 when (q − 1) ∤ w.

The gauge equation is the twisted system; MZ.4/twisted-system-solutions shows it has no nonzero solution unless (q − 1) | w and ε = 1, in which case any solutions are proportional over F_q(t), so the relations form a space of dimension ≤ 1 with trivial characters. The leaf coordinates determine the coefficients. Embed every support in the full finite family AS_w, assigning zero to omitted coefficients. Rational proportionality in this one ambient system specialises to K-proportionality of its relation coefficients, so the full relation space has dimension at most one. The relation with nonzero constant term constructed in the next step then excludes every nonzero homogeneous relation.

Existence when w = m(q − 1): expand Li(q − 1)^m in AS_w by MZ.2/strong-brown; since Li(q − 1) = −D_1^{−1}π̃^{q−1} (MZ.0/zeta-q-minus-one), this gives (−D_1)^{−m}π̃^w − Σ a_i Li(ε_i; s_i) = 0 with a ≠ 0. The operators of §1 preserve characters, so this expansion involves only trivial characters and is a relation of the required form (source issue E12).

Independence of AS_w: a K-relation among the Li(ε; s) of mixed characters becomes, by the period formula, a K̄-relation among the 𝔏𝔦-values; since these have one weight and are K-independent with a = 0 by the first part, MZ.3/chang-descent (a) makes them K̄-independent (source issue E12).
acceptance: For q = 2 and w = 1 the relation is 1 + D_1𝔏𝔦((1); (1))(θ) = 0, i.e. π̃ + D_1 Li(1) = 0.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.4, p. 35, and its proof, §3.3, pp. 36–42; Remark 3.5, p. 36
sources.match: Proves the statement on relations between ACMPL periods and π̃^w, using the strong Brown theorem for the existence of the relation with nonzero constant term.

nodes.title: The Hoffman-like basis of alternating polylogarithm values
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1, the ACMPL values Li(ε; s), (ε; s) ∈ AS_w, form a K-basis of AL_w; hence dim_K AL_w = s(w).
proofSteps: Independence: MZ.5/acmpl-period-relations. Spanning: MZ.2/strong-brown. Count: MZ.0/counting.
acceptance: dim_K AL_1 = q − 1, spanned by Li(ε; 1), ε ∈ F_q^×.

sources.match: Deduces that AS_w is a basis of AL_w with dim_K AL_w = s(w) from Theorems 3.4 and 1.11.

nodes.title: The dimension of alternating multiple zeta values
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1, dim_K AZ_w = s(w), and the ACMPL values Li(ε; s), (ε; s) ∈ AS_w, which lie in AZ_w, form a K-basis of AZ_w.
proofSteps: AZ_w = AL_w (MZ.2/value-bridge), and MZ.5/hoffman-basis.
acceptance: dim_K AZ_1 = q − 1; for q = 3, dim_K AZ_4 = 46; for q = 2, dim_K AZ_w = d(w).

sources.match: States dim_K AZ_w = s(w) with a Hoffman-like basis, deduced from Theorem 4.9 and Theorem 3.6.

nodes.title: The lower bound dim_K Z_w ≥ d(w) through CMPLs
nodes.statement: For every w ≥ 1, the CMPL values Li(s), s ∈ J′_w = IND_w, lie in Z_w and are K-linearly independent; hence dim_K Z_w ≥ d(w).
proofSteps: Li(s) ∈ Z_w: by the trivial-character version of MZ.2/brown-spanning every CMPL of weight w is a K-combination of Li(t), t ∈ J_w = I^T_w, and Li(t) = ζ_A(t) ∈ Z_w (MZ.0/carlitz-identity) (source issue E10: the source cites the alternating bridge, which only gives Li(s) ∈ AZ_w).
Independence: the trivial-character case of MZ.5/acmpl-period-relations.
|J′_w| = d(w) (MZ.0/counting).
acceptance: For w ≤ q this is MZ.5/thakur-basis-small-weight.

sources.match: Proves dim_K Z_w ≥ d(w) by viewing the CMPLs indexed by J′_w as ACMPLs with trivial characters.

nodes.title: Direct bounds for alternating MZVs in small weights
nodes.statement: (1) For w ≤ 2q − 2 (and also w = 2q − 1), the AMZVs ζ_A(ε; s) with (ε; s) ∈ AT^1_w = AJ^1_w span AZ_w, so dim_K AZ_w ≤ s(w) without ACMPLs. (2) For q > 2 and w ≤ 3q − 3, the AMZVs in the explicit set AT′_w are K-linearly independent, and |AT′_w| = s(w); so dim_K AZ_w ≥ s(w). Here AT′_w consists of the ζ_A(ε; s) with characters 1 over the entries q and 2q − 1 and with s ∈ I′_w: for w ≤ 2q − 2, the indices with no entry equal to q; for 2q − 1 ≤ w ≤ 3q − 3, those with no entry in {q, 2q − 1, 2q} or with exactly one consecutive pair (q − 1, q). (For q = 2 the source treats w ≤ 4 separately; there all characters are trivial, AZ_w = Z_w, and the bound is also MZ.5/thakur-basis-theorem.) With MZ.5/amzv-dimension, AT^1_w (w ≤ 2q − 2) and AT′_w (w ≤ 3q − 3) are bases of AZ_w consisting of AMZVs.
proofSteps: (1): show by induction on depth and first entry that ζ_A(ε, λ; U, q + w_1, W_−) and ζ_A(ε; U, q, W) lie in the span of AT^1_w, using the explicit expansion of B*_{ε,U}C_{λ,W}(R_ε), with U = ∅ treated by summing C_{λ,W}(R_ε) directly (source issue E20); the condition w ≤ 2q − 2 keeps the expansion short.

For (2), use strong induction on w and closure under deleting the last entry (the Note, Proposition 1.4(2)) to supply (LW). Character splitting and the rational suffix combinations reduce support: below 2q − 1 this is the two-row argument of MZ.4/two-row-system with a common root of the total character; in the range 2q − 1 ≤ w ≤ 3q − 3, Lemmas 5.2–5.5 of the Note restrict suffix weights to multiples of q − 1 and remove later nontrivial characters, apart from the explicit exceptional (q − 1,q) block.

For w = 2q − 1 the remaining prefixes are ∅, (1), (q − 1) and (q − 1,1), with the last two carrying the possible split characters. For w = 2q the shortlist is (2,q − 1,q − 1), (2,2q − 2), (q + 1,q − 1); for 2q + 1 ≤ w ≤ 3q − 3 replace these first entries by w − 2q + 2 and w − q + 1 and allow (w). The two-row endpoint shows ζ_A(q − 1,q − 1) and ζ_A(2q − 2) are not proportional, removing the double-tail candidate. Monic descent bounds the remaining root quotient by degree 3 in θ. Comparing θ^q and constant coefficients, separately at q = 3 and w = 3q − 3, forces a coefficient assumed in the support to vanish (the Note §§5.6–5.8, pp. 22–29).
|AT^1_w| = s(w) (MZ.0/counting) and |AT′_w| = s(w) (the Note, Proposition 1.4).
acceptance: For q = 3 and w = 4 ≤ 2q − 2, AT^1_4 has 46 elements and is a basis of AZ_4.

sources.locator: Proposition 4.11 and its proof, pp. 55–57; Remark 4.12 and Proposition 4.13, p. 57; Remark 4.14, p. 58
sources.match: States and sketches the sharp upper bound for w ≤ 2q − 2 (also 2q − 1) and the sharp lower bound for w ≤ 3q − 3 without ACMPLs, with the sets AT^1_w and AT′_w.

sources.locator: Propositions 1.3–1.4 and Theorems 1.5–1.6, pp. 3–4; §3.2, p. 12 (bijection); §4.1, pp. 12–14; §§5.1–5.8, pp. 15–29 (the ranges used here)
sources.match: Defines AT^0_w, AT^1_w, I′_w and AT′_w, counts them, and states the independence of AT^0_w for all w and of AT′_w for 1 ≤ w ≤ 3q − 2. The proof reduces to a short support list using rational suffix periods, then solves the bounded-degree root equation; the roadmap uses only w ≤ 3q − 3.

nodes.title: An upper bound for v-adic multiple zeta values
nodes.statement: Let v be a finite place of K and Z_{v,w} the K-span of the v-adic MZVs ζ_A(s)_v of weight w (Chang–Mishiba). Then dim_K Z_{v,w} ≤ d(w) − d(w − (q − 1)), with d(0) = 1 and d(n) = 0 for n < 0; the K̄-span satisfies the same bound for dim_{K̄}.
hypotheses: v a finite place of K = F_q(θ).
proofSteps: Chang–Mishiba construct a K-algebra homomorphism Z → Z_v, ζ_A(s) ↦ ζ_A(s)_v, whose kernel contains ζ_A(q − 1) (because ζ_A(q − 1)_v = 0, Goss); this v-adic input is not planned in the atlas and is recorded as a gap.
Multiplication by the nonzero element ζ_A(q − 1) ∈ Z_{q−1} embeds Z_{w−(q−1)} into Z_w (Z ⊂ K_∞ is a domain; MZ.1/value-algebras), and its image lies in the kernel of Z_w → Z_{v,w}.
So dim Z_{v,w} ≤ dim Z_w − dim Z_{w−(q−1)} = d(w) − d(w − q + 1) by MZ.5/thakur-basis-theorem (source issue E14: the source writes a K̄-span with dim_K).
acceptance: For w < q − 1 the bound is d(w); for w = q − 1 it is d(q − 1) − 1 = 2^{q−2} − 1.

sources.locator: Corollary 1.2.7 and the paragraph before it, p. 4
sources.match: Deduces the bound for v-adic MZVs from Theorem 1.2.4 and the algebra map of Chang–Mishiba killing ζ_A(q − 1).

gaps.title: Degree monotonicity of power sums for general q (Thakur–Sheats)
gaps.detail: For every prime power q, k ≥ 1 and d ≥ 0: S_d(k) ≠ 0 and deg_θ S_{d+1}(k) < deg_θ S_d(k). Thakur 2009 proves it for q prime from his degree recursion and refers, for general q, to the minimal-decomposition formula and Sheats’s degree inequality (Sheats, J. Number Theory 71 (1998)). No roadmap plans this degree theory. It is used only for the nonvanishing of MZVs with entries > q; the end theorems use CMPL values and Thakur’s range, where nonvanishing is elementary (MZ.0/cmpl-nonvanishing, MZ.0/carlitz-identity).

gaps.title: Proof of the Anderson–Thakur interpolation formula
gaps.detail: The statement (H_sΩ^s)^{(d)}(θ) = Γ_s S_d(s)/π̃^s is taken from Chang 2014 Theorem 5.5.1 and Ngo Dac §4.2; its proof (Anderson–Thakur, Ann. of Math. 132 (1990), (3.7.3)–(3.7.4), and IMRN 2009, 2.4.1) was not reread in the design or this review; no assertion about present public availability is made. A follow-up should obtain the proof and plan its steps (the generating series of power sums in terms of the Carlitz exponential and the polynomials γ_j). The CMPL route to the end theorems (Chang–Chen–Mishiba, Im–Kim–Le–Ngo Dac–Pham) does not use it; Ngo Dac’s direct route (Theorems B, 6.2, D) and the MZ property of general MZVs do.
